2354 self.ncellpercellx = symtab.find_or_create_integer_symbol(
2355 name, tag=name).name
2356 # No. of fine cells per coarse cell in y
2357 name = f"ncpc_{fine_arg.name}_{coarse_arg.name}_y"
2358 self.ncellpercelly = symtab.find_or_create_integer_symbol(
2359 name, tag=name).name
2360 # Name for cell map
2361 base_name = "cell_map_" + coarse_arg.name
2362 sym = symtab.find_or_create_array(base_name, 3,
2363 ScalarType.Intrinsic.INTEGER,
2364 tag=base_name)
2365 self.cell_map = sym.name
2366
2367 # We have no colourmap information when first created
2368 self._colourmap_symbol = None
2369 # Symbol for the variable holding the number of colours
2370 self._ncolours_var_symbol = None
2371 # Symbol of the variable holding the last cell of a particular colour.
2372 # Will be a 2D array if the kernel iteration space includes the halo
2373 # and 1D otherwise.
2374 self._last_cell_var_symbol = None
2375
2376 def set_colour_info(self, colour_map, ncolours, last_cell):
2377 '''Sets the colour_map, number of colours, and
2378 last cell of a particular colour.
2379
2380 :param colour_map: the colour map symbol.
2381 :type: colour_map:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2382 :param ncolours: the number of colours.
2383 :type: ncolours: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2384 :param last_cell: the last halo cell of a particular colour.
2385 :type last_cell: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2386
2387 '''
2388 self._colourmap_symbol = colour_map
2389 self._ncolours_var_symbol = ncolours
2390 self._last_cell_var_symbol = last_cell
2391
2392 @property
2393 def colourmap_symbol(self):
2394 ''':returns: the colour map symbol.
2395 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2396 '''
2397 return self._colourmap_symbol
2398
2399 @property
2400 def ncolours_var_symbol(self):
2401 ''':returns: the symbol for storing the number of colours.
2402 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2403 '''
2404 return self._ncolours_var_symbol
2405
2406 @property
2407 def last_cell_var_symbol(self):
2408 ''':returns: the last halo/edge cell variable.
2409 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.Symbol`
2410 '''
2411 return self._last_cell_var_symbol

2414class DynBasisFunctions(LFRicCollection):
2415 ''' Holds all information on the basis and differential basis
2416 functions required by an invoke or kernel call. This covers both those
2417 required for quadrature and for evaluators.
2418
2419 :param node: either the schedule of an Invoke or a single Kernel object
2420 for which to extract information on all required
2421 basis/diff-basis functions.
2422 :type node: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicInvokeSchedule` or
2423 :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
2424
2425 :raises InternalError: if a call has an unrecognised evaluator shape.
2426
2427 '''
2428 # Dimensioning vars for the basis function arrays required by each
2429 # type of quadrature
2430 qr_dim_vars = {"xyoz": ["np_xy", "np_z"],
2431 "edge": ["np_xyz", "nedges"],
2432 "face": ["np_xyz", "nfaces"]}
2433 # The different weights arrays required by each type of quadrature
2434 qr_weight_vars = {"xyoz": ["weights_xy", "weights_z"],
2435 "edge": ["weights_xyz"],
2436 "face": ["weights_xyz"]}
2437
2438 def __init__(self, node):
2439
2440 super().__init__(node)
2441
2442 # Construct a list of all the basis/diff-basis functions required
2443 # by this invoke. Each entry in the list is a dictionary holding
2444 # the shape, the function space and the 'target' function spaces
2445 # (upon which the basis functions are evaluated).
2446 self._basis_fns_basis_fns = []
2447 # The dictionary of quadrature objects passed to this invoke. Keys
2448 # are the various VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES, values are a list of
2449 # associated quadrature variables. (i.e. we have a list of
2450 # quadrature arguments for each shape.)
2451 self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars = OrderedDict()
2452 # The dict of target function spaces upon which we must provide
2453 # evaluators. Keys are the FS names, values are (FunctionSpace,
2454 # DynKernelArgument) tuples.
2455 self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets = OrderedDict()
2456
2457 for call in self._calls_calls:
2458
2459 if isinstance(call, LFRicBuiltIn) or not call.eval_shapes:
2460 # Skip this kernel if it doesn't require basis/diff basis fns
2461 continue
2462
2463 for shape, rule in call.qr_rules.items():
2464
2465 # This kernel requires quadrature
2466 if shape not in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars:
2467 # We haven't seen a quadrature arg with this shape
2468 # before so create a dictionary entry with an
2469 # empty list
2470 self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape] = []
2471 if rule.psy_name not in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape]:
2472 # Add this qr argument to the list of those that
2473 # have this shape
2474 self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape].append(rule.psy_name)
2475
2476 if "gh_evaluator" in call.eval_shapes:
2477 # An evaluator consists of basis or diff basis functions
2478 # for one FS evaluated on the nodes of another 'target' FS.
2479 # Make a dict of 2-tuples, each containing the
2480 # FunctionSpace and associated kernel argument for the
2481 # target FSs.
2482
2483 # Loop over the target FS for evaluators required by this
2484 # kernel
2485 for fs_name in call.eval_targets:
2486 if fs_name not in self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets:
2487 # We don't already have this space in our list so
2488 # add it to the list of target spaces
2489 self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets[fs_name] = \
2490 call.eval_targets[fs_name]
2491
2492 # Both quadrature and evaluators require basis and/or differential
2493 # basis functions. This helper routine populates self._basis_fns
2494 # with entries describing the basis functions required by
2495 # this call.
2496 self._setup_basis_fns_for_call(call)
2497
2498 @staticmethod
2499 def basis_first_dim_name(function_space):
2500 '''
2501 Get the name of the variable holding the first dimension of a
2502 basis function
2503
2504 :param function_space: the function space the basis function is for
2505 :type function_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
2506 :return: a Fortran variable name
2507 :rtype: str
2508
2509 '''
2510 return "dim_" + function_space.mangled_name
2511
2512 @staticmethod
2513 def basis_first_dim_value(function_space):
2514 '''
2515 Get the size of the first dimension of a basis function.
2516
2517 :param function_space: the function space the basis function is for
2518 :type function_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
2519 :return: an integer length.
2520 :rtype: string
2521
2522 :raises GenerationError: if an unsupported function space is supplied \
2523 (e.g. ANY_SPACE_*, ANY_DISCONTINUOUS_SPACE_*)
2524 '''
2525 if function_space.has_scalar_basis:
2526 first_dim = "1"
2527 elif function_space.has_vector_basis:
2528 first_dim = "3"
2529 else:
2530 # It is not possible to determine explicitly the first basis
2531 # function array dimension from the metadata for any_space or
2532 # any_discontinuous_space. This information needs to be passed
2533 # from the PSy layer to the kernels (see issue #461).
2534 const = LFRicConstants()
2535 raise GenerationError(
2536 f"Unsupported space for basis function, "
2537 f"expecting one of {const.VALID_FUNCTION_SPACES} but found "
2538 f"'{function_space.orig_name}'")
2539 return first_dim
2540
2541 @staticmethod
2542 def diff_basis_first_dim_name(function_space):
2543 '''
2544 Get the name of the variable holding the first dimension of a
2545 differential basis function.
2546
2547 :param function_space: the function space the diff-basis function \
2548 is for.
2549 :type function_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
2550 :return: a Fortran variable name.
2551 :rtype: str
2552
2553 '''
2554 return "diff_dim_" + function_space.mangled_name
2555
2556 @staticmethod
2557 def diff_basis_first_dim_value(function_space):
2558 '''
2559 Get the size of the first dimension of an array for a
2560 differential basis function.
2561
2562 :param function_space: the function space the diff-basis function \
2563 is for.
2564 :type function_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
2565 :return: an integer length.
2566 :rtype: str
2567
2568 :raises GenerationError: if an unsupported function space is \
2569 supplied (e.g. ANY_SPACE_*, \
2570 ANY_DISCONTINUOUS_SPACE_*)
2571
2572 '''
2573 if function_space.has_scalar_diff_basis:
2574 first_dim = "1"
2575 elif function_space.has_vector_diff_basis:
2576 first_dim = "3"
2577 else:
2578 # It is not possible to determine explicitly the first
2579 # differential basis function array dimension from the metadata
2580 # for any_space or any_discontinuous_space. This information
2581 # needs to be passed from the PSy layer to the kernels
2582 # (see issue #461).
2583 const = LFRicConstants()
2584 raise GenerationError(
2585 f"Unsupported space for differential basis function, "
2586 f"expecting one of {const.VALID_FUNCTION_SPACES} but found "
2587 f"'{function_space.orig_name}'")
2588 return first_dim
2589
2590 def _setup_basis_fns_for_call(self, call):
2591 '''
2592 Populates self._basis_fns with entries describing the basis
2593 functions required by the supplied Call.
2594
2595 :param call: the kernel call for which basis functions are required.
2596 :type call: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
2597
2598 :raises InternalError: if the supplied call is of incorrect type.
2599 :raises InternalError: if the supplied call has an unrecognised \
2600 evaluator shape.
2601 '''
2602 if not isinstance(call, LFRicKern):
2603 raise InternalError(f"Expected a LFRicKern object but got: "
2604 f"'{type(call)}'")
2605 const = LFRicConstants()
2606 # We need a full FunctionSpace object for each function space
2607 # that has basis functions associated with it.
2608 for fsd in call.fs_descriptors.descriptors:
2609
2610 # We need the full FS object, not just the name. Therefore
2611 # we first have to get a kernel argument that is on this
2612 # space...
2613 arg, fspace = call.arguments.get_arg_on_space_name(fsd.fs_name)
2614
2615 for shape in call.eval_shapes:
2616
2617 # Populate a dict with the shape, function space and
2618 # associated kernel argument for this basis/diff-basis f'n.
2619 entry = {"shape": shape,
2620 "fspace": fspace,
2621 "arg": arg}
2622 if shape in const.VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES:
2623 # This is for quadrature - store the name of the
2624 # qr variable
2625 entry["qr_var"] = call.qr_rules[shape].psy_name
2626 # Quadrature weights are evaluated at pre-determined
2627 # points rather than at the nodes of another FS.
2628 # We put one entry of None in the list of target
2629 # spaces to facilitate cases where we loop over
2630 # this list.
2631 entry["nodal_fspaces"] = [None]
2632 elif shape == "gh_evaluator":
2633 # This is an evaluator
2634 entry["qr_var"] = None
2635 # Store a list of the FunctionSpace objects for which
2636 # these basis functions are to be evaluated
2637 entry["nodal_fspaces"] = [items[0] for items in
2638 call.eval_targets.values()]
2639 else:
2640 raise InternalError(f"Unrecognised evaluator shape: "
2641 f"'{shape}'. Should be one of "
2642 f"{const.VALID_EVALUATOR_SHAPES}")
2643
2644 # Add our newly-constructed dict object to the list describing
2645 # the required basis and/or differential basis functions for
2646 # this Invoke.
2647 if fsd.requires_basis:
2648 entry["type"] = "basis"
2649 self._basis_fns_basis_fns.append(entry)
2650 if fsd.requires_diff_basis:
2651 # Take a shallow copy of the dict and just modify the
2652 # 'type' of the basis function it describes (this works
2653 # because the 'type' entry is a primitive type [str]).
2654 diff_entry = entry.copy()
2655 diff_entry["type"] = "diff-basis"
2656 self._basis_fns_basis_fns.append(diff_entry)
2657
2658 def _stub_declarations(self, parent):
2659 '''
2660 Insert the variable declarations required by the basis functions into
2661 the Kernel stub.
2662
2663 :param parent: the f2pygen node representing the Kernel stub.
2664 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
2665
2666 :raises InternalError: if an unsupported quadrature shape is found.
2667
2668 '''
2669 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
2670
2671 if not self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars and not self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets:
2672 return
2673
2674 # The quadrature shapes that this method supports
2675 supported_shapes = ["gh_quadrature_xyoz", "gh_quadrature_face",
2676 "gh_quadrature_edge"]
2677
2678 # Get the lists of dimensioning variables and basis arrays
2679 var_dims, basis_arrays = self._basis_fn_declns()
2680
2681 if var_dims:
2682 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
2683 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
2684 intent="in", entity_decls=var_dims))
2685 for basis in basis_arrays:
2686 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="real",
2687 kind=api_config.default_kind["real"],
2688 intent="in",
2689 dimension=",".join(basis_arrays[basis]),
2690 entity_decls=[basis]))
2691
2692 const = LFRicConstants()
2693
2694 for shape in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars:
2695 qr_name = "_qr_" + shape.split("_")[-1]
2696 if shape == "gh_quadrature_xyoz":
2697 datatype = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["intrinsic"]
2698 kind = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["kind"]
2699 parent.add(DeclGen(
2700 parent, datatype=datatype, kind=kind,
2701 intent="in", dimension="np_xy"+qr_name,
2702 entity_decls=["weights_xy"+qr_name]))
2703 parent.add(DeclGen(
2704 parent, datatype=datatype, kind=kind,
2705 intent="in", dimension="np_z"+qr_name,
2706 entity_decls=["weights_z"+qr_name]))
2707 elif shape == "gh_quadrature_face":
2708 parent.add(DeclGen(
2709 parent,
2710 datatype=const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["intrinsic"],
2711 kind=const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["kind"], intent="in",
2712 dimension=",".join(["np_xyz"+qr_name, "nfaces"+qr_name]),
2713 entity_decls=["weights_xyz"+qr_name]))
2714 elif shape == "gh_quadrature_edge":
2715 parent.add(DeclGen(
2716 parent,
2717 datatype=const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["intrinsic"],
2718 kind=const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["kind"], intent="in",
2719 dimension=",".join(["np_xyz"+qr_name, "nedges"+qr_name]),
2720 entity_decls=["weights_xyz"+qr_name]))
2721 else:
2722 raise InternalError(
2723 f"Quadrature shapes other than {supported_shapes} are not "
2724 f"yet supported - got: '{shape}'")
2725
2726 def _invoke_declarations(self, parent):
2727 '''
2728 Add basis-function declarations to the PSy layer.
2729
2730 :param parent: f2pygen node represening the PSy-layer routine.
2731 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
2732
2733 '''
2734 # Create a single declaration for each quadrature type
2735 const = LFRicConstants()
2736 for shape in const.VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES:
2737 if shape in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars and self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape]:
2738 # The PSy-layer routine is passed objects of
2739 # quadrature_* type
2740 parent.add(
2741 TypeDeclGen(parent,
2742 datatype=const.
2743 QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["type"],
2744 entity_decls=self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape],
2745 intent="in"))
2746 # For each of these we'll need a corresponding proxy, use
2747 # the symbol_table to avoid clashes...
2748 var_names = []
2749 for var in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars[shape]:
2750 var_names.append(
2751 self._symbol_table.find_or_create_tag(var+"_proxy")
2752 .name)
2753 parent.add(
2754 TypeDeclGen(
2755 parent,
2756 datatype=const.
2757 QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shape]["proxy_type"],
2758 entity_decls=var_names))
2759
2760 def initialise(self, parent):
2761 '''
2762 Create the declarations and assignments required for the
2763 basis-functions required by an invoke. These are added as children
2764 of the supplied parent node in the AST.
2765
2766 :param parent: the node in the f2pygen AST that will be the
2767 parent of all of the declarations and assignments.
2768 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
2769
2770 :raises InternalError: if an invalid entry is encountered in the \
2771 self._basis_fns list.
2772 '''
2773 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches, too-many-locals
2774 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
2775 const = LFRicConstants()
2776 basis_declarations = []
2777
2778 # We need BASIS and/or DIFF_BASIS if any kernel requires quadrature
2779 # or an evaluator
2780 if self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars or self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets:
2781 parent.add(
2782 UseGen(parent, name=const.
2783 FUNCTION_SPACE_TYPE_MAP["function_space"]["module"],
2784 only=True, funcnames=["BASIS", "DIFF_BASIS"]))
2785
2786 if self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars:
2787 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2788 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, " Look-up quadrature variables"))
2789 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2790
2791 # Look-up the module- and type-names from the QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP
2792 for shp in self._qr_vars_qr_vars_qr_vars:
2793 quad_map = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[shp]
2794 parent.add(UseGen(parent,
2795 name=quad_map["module"],
2796 only=True,
2797 funcnames=[quad_map["type"],
2798 quad_map["proxy_type"]]))
2799 self._initialise_xyz_qr(parent)
2800 self._initialise_xyoz_qr(parent)
2801 self._initialise_xoyoz_qr(parent)
2802 self._initialise_face_or_edge_qr(parent, "face")
2803 self._initialise_face_or_edge_qr(parent, "edge")
2804
2805 if self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets:
2806 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2807 parent.add(CommentGen(parent,
2808 " Initialise evaluator-related quantities "
2809 "for the target function spaces"))
2810 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2811
2812 for (fspace, arg) in self._eval_targets_eval_targets_eval_targets.values():
2813 # We need the list of nodes for each unique FS upon which we need
2814 # to evaluate basis/diff-basis functions
2815 nodes_name = "nodes_" + fspace.mangled_name
2816 parent.add(AssignGen(
2817 parent, lhs=nodes_name,
2818 rhs="%".join([arg.proxy_name_indexed, arg.ref_name(fspace),
2819 "get_nodes()"]),
2820 pointer=True))
2821 my_kind = api_config.default_kind["real"]
2822 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="real",
2823 kind=my_kind,
2824 pointer=True,
2825 entity_decls=[nodes_name+"(:,:) => null()"]))
2826 const_mod = const.UTILITIES_MOD_MAP["constants"]["module"]
2827 const_mod_uses = self._invoke_invoke.invokes.psy. \
2828 infrastructure_modules[const_mod]
2829 # Record that we will need to import the kind for a
2830 # pointer declaration (associated with a function
2831 # space) from the appropriate infrastructure module
2832 const_mod_uses.add(my_kind)
2833
2834 if self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
2835 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2836 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, " Allocate basis/diff-basis arrays"))
2837 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
2838
2839 var_dim_list = []
2840 for basis_fn in self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
2841 # Get the extent of the first dimension of the basis array.
2842 if basis_fn['type'] == "basis":
2843 first_dim = self.basis_first_dim_name(basis_fn["fspace"])
2844 dim_space = "get_dim_space()"
2845 elif basis_fn['type'] == "diff-basis":
2846 first_dim = self.diff_basis_first_dim_name(
2847 basis_fn["fspace"])
2848 dim_space = "get_dim_space_diff()"
2849 else:
2850 raise InternalError(
2851 f"Unrecognised type of basis function: "
2852 f"'{basis_fn['''type''']}'. Should be either 'basis' or "
2853 f"'diff-basis'.")
2854
2855 if first_dim not in var_dim_list:
2856 var_dim_list.append(first_dim)
2857 rhs = "%".join(
2858 [basis_fn["arg"].proxy_name_indexed,
2859 basis_fn["arg"].ref_name(basis_fn["fspace"]),
2860 dim_space])
2861 parent.add(AssignGen(parent, lhs=first_dim, rhs=rhs))
2862
2863 var_dims, basis_arrays = self._basis_fn_declns()
2864
2865 if var_dims:
2866 # declare dim and diff_dim for all function spaces
2867 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
2868 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
2869 entity_decls=var_dims))
2870
2871 basis_declarations = []
2872 for basis in basis_arrays:
2873 parent.add(
2874 AllocateGen(parent,
2875 basis+"("+", ".join(basis_arrays[basis])+")"))
2876 basis_declarations.append(
2877 basis+"("+",".join([":"]*len(basis_arrays[basis]))+")")
2878
2879 # declare the basis function arrays
2880 if basis_declarations:
2881 my_kind = api_config.default_kind["real"]
2882 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="real", kind=my_kind,
2883 allocatable=True,
2884 entity_decls=basis_declarations))
2885 # Default kind (r_def) will always already exist due to
2886 # arrays associated with gh_shape, so there is no need to
2887 # declare it here.
2888
2889 # Compute the values for any basis arrays
2890 self._compute_basis_fns(parent)
2891
2892 def _basis_fn_declns(self):
2893 '''
2894 Extracts all information relating to the necessary declarations
2895 for basis-function arrays.
2896
2897 :returns: a 2-tuple containing a list of dimensioning variables & a \
2898 dict of basis arrays.
2899 :rtype: (list of str, dict)
2900
2901 :raises InternalError: if neither self._invoke or self._kernel are set.
2902 :raises InternalError: if an unrecognised type of basis function is \
2903 encountered.
2904 :raises InternalError: if an unrecognised evaluator shape is \
2905 encountered.
2906 :raises InternalError: if there is no name for the quadrature object \
2907 when generating PSy-layer code.
2908
2909 '''
2910 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
2911 # Dictionary of basis arrays where key values are the array names and
2912 # entries are a list of dimensions.
2913 basis_arrays = OrderedDict()
2914 # List of names of dimensioning (scalar) variables
2915 var_dim_list = []
2916
2917 const = LFRicConstants()
2918 # Loop over the list of dicts describing each basis function
2919 # required by this Invoke.
2920 for basis_fn in self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
2921 # Get the extent of the first dimension of the basis array and
2922 # store whether we have a basis or a differential basis function.
2923 # Currently there are only those two possible types of basis
2924 # function and we store the required diff basis name in basis_name.
2925 if basis_fn['type'] == "basis":
2926 if self._invoke_invoke:
2927 first_dim = self.basis_first_dim_name(basis_fn["fspace"])
2928 elif self._kernel_kernel:
2929 first_dim = self.basis_first_dim_value(basis_fn["fspace"])
2930 else:
2931 raise InternalError("Require basis functions but do not "
2932 "have either a Kernel or an "
2933 "Invoke. Should be impossible.")
2934 basis_name = "gh_basis"
2935 elif basis_fn['type'] == "diff-basis":
2936 if self._invoke_invoke:
2937 first_dim = self.diff_basis_first_dim_name(
2938 basis_fn["fspace"])
2939 elif self._kernel_kernel:
2940 first_dim = self.diff_basis_first_dim_value(
2941 basis_fn["fspace"])
2942 else:
2943 raise InternalError("Require differential basis functions "
2944 "but do not have either a Kernel or "
2945 "an Invoke. Should be impossible.")
2946 basis_name = "gh_diff_basis"
2947 else:
2948 raise InternalError(
2949 f"Unrecognised type of basis function: "
2950 f"'{basis_fn['''type''']}'. Should be either 'basis' or "
2951 f"'diff-basis'.")
2952
2953 if self._invoke_invoke and first_dim not in var_dim_list:
2954 var_dim_list.append(first_dim)
2955
2956 if basis_fn["shape"] in const.VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES:
2957
2958 qr_var = basis_fn["qr_var"]
2959 if not qr_var:
2960 raise InternalError(
2961 f"Quadrature '{basis_fn['''shape''']}' is required but"
2962 f" have no name for the associated Quadrature object.")
2963
2964 op_name = basis_fn["fspace"].get_operator_name(basis_name,
2965 qr_var=qr_var)
2966 if op_name in basis_arrays:
2967 # We've already seen a basis with this name so skip
2968 continue
2969
2970 # Dimensionality of the basis arrays depends on the
2971 # type of quadrature...
2972 alloc_args = qr_basis_alloc_args(first_dim, basis_fn)
2973 for arg in alloc_args:
2974 # In a kernel stub the first dimension of the array is
2975 # a numerical value so make sure we don't try and declare
2976 # it as a variable.
2977 if not arg[0].isdigit() and arg not in var_dim_list:
2978 var_dim_list.append(arg)
2979 basis_arrays[op_name] = alloc_args
2980
2981 elif basis_fn["shape"].lower() == "gh_evaluator":
2982 # This is an evaluator and thus may be required on more than
2983 # one function space
2984 for target_space in basis_fn["nodal_fspaces"]:
2985 op_name = basis_fn["fspace"].\
2986 get_operator_name(basis_name,
2987 qr_var=basis_fn["qr_var"],
2988 on_space=target_space)
2989 if op_name in basis_arrays:
2990 continue
2991 # We haven't seen a basis with this name before so
2992 # need to store its dimensions
2993 basis_arrays[op_name] = [
2994 first_dim,
2995 basis_fn["fspace"].ndf_name,
2996 target_space.ndf_name]
2997 else:
2998 raise InternalError(
2999 f"Unrecognised evaluator shape: '{basis_fn['''shape''']}'."
3000 f" Should be one of {const.VALID_EVALUATOR_SHAPES}")
3001
3002 return (var_dim_list, basis_arrays)
3003

3007 quadrature

3010 in which to insert the initialisation

3018 def _initialise_xyoz_qr(self, parent):
3019 '''
3020 Add in the initialisation of variables needed for XYoZ
3021 quadrature
3022
3023 :param parent: the node in the AST representing the PSy subroutine
3024 in which to insert the initialisation
3025 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
3026
3027 '''
3028 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
3029
3030 if "gh_quadrature_xyoz" not in self._qr_vars:
3031 return
3032
3033 for qr_arg_name in self._qr_vars["gh_quadrature_xyoz"]:
3034
3035 # We generate unique names for the integers holding the numbers
3036 # of quadrature points by appending the name of the quadrature
3037 # argument
3038 parent.add(
3039 DeclGen(
3040 parent, datatype="integer",
3041 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
3042 entity_decls=[name+"_"+qr_arg_name
3043 for name in self.qr_dim_vars["xyoz"]]))
3044 decl_list = [name+"_"+qr_arg_name+"(:) => null()"
3045 for name in self.qr_weight_vars["xyoz"]]
3046 const = LFRicConstants()
3047 datatype = \
3048 const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP["gh_quadrature_xyoz"]["intrinsic"]
3049 kind = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP["gh_quadrature_xyoz"]["kind"]
3050 parent.add(
3051 DeclGen(parent, datatype=datatype, kind=kind,
3052 pointer=True, entity_decls=decl_list))
3053 const_mod = const.UTILITIES_MOD_MAP["constants"]["module"]
3054 const_mod_uses = self._invoke.invokes.psy. \
3055 infrastructure_modules[const_mod]
3056 # Record that we will need to import the kind for a
3057 # declaration (associated with quadrature) from
3058 # the appropriate infrastructure module
3059 const_mod_uses.add(kind)
3060
3061 # Get the quadrature proxy
3062 proxy_name = qr_arg_name + "_proxy"
3063 parent.add(
3064 AssignGen(parent, lhs=proxy_name,
3065 rhs=qr_arg_name+"%"+"get_quadrature_proxy()"))
3066 # Number of points in each dimension
3067 for qr_var in self.qr_dim_vars["xyoz"]:
3068 parent.add(
3069 AssignGen(parent, lhs=qr_var+"_"+qr_arg_name,
3070 rhs=proxy_name+"%"+qr_var))
3071 # Pointers to the weights arrays
3072 for qr_var in self.qr_weight_vars["xyoz"]:
3073 parent.add(
3074 AssignGen(parent, pointer=True,
3075 lhs=qr_var+"_"+qr_arg_name,
3076 rhs=proxy_name+"%"+qr_var))
3077

3080 Add in the initialisation of variables needed for XoYoZ
3081 quadrature.

3092 def _initialise_face_or_edge_qr(self, parent, qr_type):
3093 '''
3094 Add in the initialisation of variables needed for face or edge
3095 quadrature.
3096
3097 :param parent: the node in the AST representing the PSy subroutine \
3098 in which to insert the initialisation.
3099 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
3100 :param str qr_type: whether to generate initialisation code for \
3101 "face" or "edge" quadrature.
3102
3103 :raises InternalError: if `qr_type` is not "face" or "edge".
3104
3105 '''
3106 if qr_type not in ["face", "edge"]:
3107 raise InternalError(
3108 f"_initialise_face_or_edge_qr: qr_type argument must be "
3109 f"either 'face' or 'edge' but got: '{qr_type}'")
3110
3111 quadrature_name = f"gh_quadrature_{qr_type}"
3112
3113 if quadrature_name not in self._qr_vars:
3114 return
3115
3116 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
3117 symbol_table = self._symbol_table
3118
3119 for qr_arg_name in self._qr_vars[quadrature_name]:
3120 # We generate unique names for the integers holding the numbers
3121 # of quadrature points by appending the name of the quadrature
3122 # argument
3123 decl_list = [
3124 symbol_table.find_or_create_integer_symbol(
3125 name+"_"+qr_arg_name, tag=name+"_"+qr_arg_name).name
3126 for name in self.qr_dim_vars[qr_type]]
3127 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
3128 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
3129 entity_decls=decl_list))
3130
3131 names = [f"{name}_{qr_arg_name}"
3132 for name in self.qr_weight_vars[qr_type]]
3133 decl_list = [
3134 symbol_table.find_or_create_array(name, 2,
3135 ScalarType.Intrinsic.REAL,
3136 tag=name).name
3137 + "(:,:) => null()" for name in names]
3138 const = LFRicConstants()
3139 datatype = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[quadrature_name]["intrinsic"]
3140 kind = const.QUADRATURE_TYPE_MAP[quadrature_name]["kind"]
3141 parent.add(
3142 DeclGen(parent, datatype=datatype, pointer=True, kind=kind,
3143 entity_decls=decl_list))
3144 const_mod = const.UTILITIES_MOD_MAP["constants"]["module"]
3145 const_mod_uses = self._invoke.invokes.psy. \
3146 infrastructure_modules[const_mod]
3147 # Record that we will need to import the kind for a
3148 # declaration (associated with quadrature) from the
3149 # appropriate infrastructure module
3150 const_mod_uses.add(kind)
3151 # Get the quadrature proxy
3152 proxy_name = symbol_table.find_or_create_tag(
3153 qr_arg_name+"_proxy").name
3154 parent.add(
3155 AssignGen(parent, lhs=proxy_name,
3156 rhs=qr_arg_name+"%"+"get_quadrature_proxy()"))
3157 # The dimensioning variables required for this quadrature
3158 # (e.g. nedges/nfaces, np_xyz)
3159 for qr_var in self.qr_dim_vars[qr_type]:
3160 parent.add(
3161 AssignGen(parent, lhs=qr_var+"_"+qr_arg_name,
3162 rhs=proxy_name+"%"+qr_var))
3163 # Pointers to the weights arrays
3164 for qr_var in self.qr_weight_vars[qr_type]:
3165 parent.add(
3166 AssignGen(parent, pointer=True,
3167 lhs=qr_var+"_"+qr_arg_name,
3168 rhs=proxy_name+"%"+qr_var))
3169
3170 def _compute_basis_fns(self, parent):
3171 '''
3172 Generates the necessary Fortran to compute the values of
3173 any basis/diff-basis arrays required
3174
3175 :param parent: Node in the f2pygen AST which will be the parent
3176 of the assignments created in this routine
3177 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
3178
3179 '''
3180 # pylint: disable=too-many-locals
3181 const = LFRicConstants()
3182 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
3183
3184 loop_var_list = set()
3185 op_name_list = []
3186 # add calls to compute the values of any basis arrays
3187 if self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
3188 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
3189 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, " Compute basis/diff-basis arrays"))
3190 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
3191
3192 for basis_fn in self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
3193
3194 # Currently there are only two possible types of basis function
3195 # and we store the corresponding strings to use in basis_name,
3196 # basis_type, and first_dim. If support for other basis function
3197 # types is added in future then more tests need to be added here.
3198 if basis_fn["type"] == "diff-basis":
3199 basis_name = "gh_diff_basis"
3200 basis_type = "DIFF_BASIS"
3201 first_dim = self.diff_basis_first_dim_name(basis_fn["fspace"])
3202 elif basis_fn["type"] == "basis":
3203 basis_name = "gh_basis"
3204 basis_type = "BASIS"
3205 first_dim = self.basis_first_dim_name(basis_fn["fspace"])
3206 else:
3207 raise InternalError(
3208 f"Unrecognised type of basis function: "
3209 f"'{basis_fn['''type''']}'. Expected one of 'basis' or "
3210 f"'diff-basis'.")
3211 if basis_fn["shape"] in const.VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES:
3212 op_name = basis_fn["fspace"].\
3213 get_operator_name(basis_name, qr_var=basis_fn["qr_var"])
3214 if op_name in op_name_list:
3215 # Jump over any basis arrays we've seen before
3216 continue
3217 op_name_list.append(op_name)
3218
3219 # Create the argument list
3220 args = [basis_type, basis_fn["arg"].proxy_name_indexed + "%" +
3221 basis_fn["arg"].ref_name(basis_fn["fspace"]),
3222 first_dim, basis_fn["fspace"].ndf_name, op_name]
3223
3224 # insert the basis array call
3225 parent.add(
3226 CallGen(parent,
3227 name=basis_fn["qr_var"]+"%compute_function",
3228 args=args))
3229 elif basis_fn["shape"].lower() == "gh_evaluator":
3230 # We have an evaluator. We may need this on more than one
3231 # function space.
3232 for space in basis_fn["nodal_fspaces"]:
3233 op_name = basis_fn["fspace"].\
3234 get_operator_name(basis_name, on_space=space)
3235 if op_name in op_name_list:
3236 # Jump over any basis arrays we've seen before
3237 continue
3238 op_name_list.append(op_name)
3239
3240 nodal_loop_var = "df_nodal"
3241 loop_var_list.add(nodal_loop_var)
3242
3243 # Loop over dofs of target function space
3244 nodal_dof_loop = DoGen(
3245 parent, nodal_loop_var, "1", space.ndf_name)
3246 parent.add(nodal_dof_loop)
3247
3248 dof_loop_var = "df_" + basis_fn["fspace"].mangled_name
3249 loop_var_list.add(dof_loop_var)
3250
3251 dof_loop = DoGen(nodal_dof_loop, dof_loop_var,
3252 "1", basis_fn["fspace"].ndf_name)
3253 nodal_dof_loop.add(dof_loop)
3254 lhs = op_name + "(:," + "df_" + \
3255 basis_fn["fspace"].mangled_name + "," + "df_nodal)"
3256 rhs = (f"{basis_fn['arg'].proxy_name_indexed}%"
3257 f"{basis_fn['arg'].ref_name(basis_fn['fspace'])}%"
3258 f"call_function({basis_type},{dof_loop_var},nodes_"
3259 f"{space.mangled_name}(:,{nodal_loop_var}))")
3260 dof_loop.add(AssignGen(dof_loop, lhs=lhs, rhs=rhs))
3261 else:
3262 raise InternalError(
3263 f"Unrecognised shape '{basis_fn['''shape''']}' specified "
3264 f"for basis function. Should be one of: "
3265 f"{const.VALID_EVALUATOR_SHAPES}")
3266 if loop_var_list:
3267 # Declare any loop variables
3268 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
3269 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
3270 entity_decls=sorted(loop_var_list)))
3271
3272 def deallocate(self, parent):
3273 '''
3274 Add code to deallocate all basis/diff-basis function arrays
3275
3276 :param parent: node in the f2pygen AST to which the deallocate \
3277 calls will be added.
3278 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
3279
3280 :raises InternalError: if an unrecognised type of basis function \
3281 is encountered.
3282 '''
3283 if self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
3284 # deallocate all allocated basis function arrays
3285 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
3286 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, " Deallocate basis arrays"))
3287 parent.add(CommentGen(parent, ""))
3288
3289 func_space_var_names = set()
3290 for basis_fn in self._basis_fns_basis_fns:
3291 # add the basis array name to the list to use later
3292 if basis_fn["type"] == "basis":
3293 basis_name = "gh_basis"
3294 elif basis_fn["type"] == "diff-basis":
3295 basis_name = "gh_diff_basis"
3296 else:
3297 raise InternalError(
3298 f"Unrecognised type of basis function: "
3299 f"'{basis_fn['''type''']}'. Should be one of 'basis' or "
3300 f"'diff-basis'.")
3301 for fspace in basis_fn["nodal_fspaces"]:
3302 op_name = basis_fn["fspace"].\
3303 get_operator_name(basis_name,
3304 qr_var=basis_fn["qr_var"],
3305 on_space=fspace)
3306 func_space_var_names.add(op_name)
3307
3308 if func_space_var_names:
3309 # add the required deallocate call
3310 parent.add(DeallocateGen(parent, sorted(func_space_var_names)))
3311
3312
3313class DynBoundaryConditions(LFRicCollection):
3314 '''
3315 Manages declarations and initialisation of quantities required by
3316 kernels that need boundary condition information.
3317
3318 :param node: the Invoke or Kernel stub for which we are to handle \
3319 any boundary conditions.
3320 :type node: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.LFRicInvoke` or \
3321 :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
3322
3323 :raises GenerationError: if a kernel named "enforce_bc_code" is found \
3324 but does not have an argument on ANY_SPACE_1.
3325 :raises GenerationError: if a kernel named "enforce_operator_bc_code" is \
3326 found but does not have exactly one argument.
3327 '''
3328 # Define a BoundaryDofs namedtuple to help us manage the arrays that
3329 # are required.
3330 BoundaryDofs = namedtuple("BoundaryDofs", ["argument", "function_space"])
3331
3332 def __init__(self, node):
3333 super().__init__(node)
3334
3335 self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs = []
3336 # Check through all the kernel calls to see whether any of them
3337 # require boundary conditions. Currently this is done by recognising
3338 # the kernel name.
3339 # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
3340 from psyclone.domain.lfric.metadata_to_arguments_rules import (
3341 MetadataToArgumentsRules)
3342 for call in self._calls_calls:
3343 if MetadataToArgumentsRules.bc_kern_regex.match(call.name):
3344 bc_fs = None
3345 for fspace in call.arguments.unique_fss:
3346 if fspace.orig_name == "any_space_1":
3347 bc_fs = fspace
3348 break
3349 if not bc_fs:
3350 raise GenerationError(
3351 "The enforce_bc_code kernel must have an argument on "
3352 "ANY_SPACE_1 but failed to find such an argument.")
3353 farg = call.arguments.get_arg_on_space(bc_fs)
3354 self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs.append(self.BoundaryDofs(farg, bc_fs))
3355 elif call.name.lower() == "enforce_operator_bc_code":
3356 # Check that the kernel only has one argument
3357 if len(call.arguments.args) != 1:
3358 raise GenerationError(
3359 f"The enforce_operator_bc_code kernel must have "
3360 f"exactly one argument but found "
3361 f"{len(call.arguments.args)}")
3362 op_arg = call.arguments.args[0]
3363 bc_fs = op_arg.function_space_to
3364 self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs.append(self.BoundaryDofs(op_arg, bc_fs))
3365
3366 def _invoke_declarations(self, parent):
3367 '''
3368 Add declarations for any boundary-dofs arrays required by an Invoke.
3369
3370 :param parent: node in the PSyIR to which to add declarations.
3371 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3372
3373 '''
3374 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
3375
3376 for dofs in self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs:
3377 name = "boundary_dofs_" + dofs.argument.name
3378 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
3379 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
3380 pointer=True,
3381 entity_decls=[name+"(:,:) => null()"]))
3382
3383 def _stub_declarations(self, parent):
3384 '''
3385 Add declarations for any boundary-dofs arrays required by a kernel.
3386
3387 :param parent: node in the PSyIR to which to add declarations.
3388 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3389
3390 '''
3391 api_config = Config.get().api_conf("lfric")
3392
3393 for dofs in self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs:
3394 name = "boundary_dofs_" + dofs.argument.name
3395 ndf_name = dofs.function_space.ndf_name
3396 parent.add(DeclGen(parent, datatype="integer",
3397 kind=api_config.default_kind["integer"],
3398 intent="in",
3399 dimension=",".join([ndf_name, "2"]),
3400 entity_decls=[name]))
3401
3402 def initialise(self, parent):
3403 '''
3404 Initialise any boundary-dofs arrays required by an Invoke.
3405
3406 :param parent: node in PSyIR to which to add declarations.
3407 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3408
3409 '''
3410 for dofs in self._boundary_dofs_boundary_dofs:
3411 name = "boundary_dofs_" + dofs.argument.name
3412 parent.add(AssignGen(
3413 parent, pointer=True, lhs=name,
3414 rhs="%".join([dofs.argument.proxy_name,
3415 dofs.argument.ref_name(dofs.function_space),
3416 "get_boundary_dofs()"])))
3417
3418
3419class DynGlobalSum(GlobalSum):
3420 '''
3421 Dynamo specific global sum class which can be added to and
3422 manipulated in a schedule.
3423
3424 :param scalar: the kernel argument for which to perform a global sum.
3425 :type scalar: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
3426 :param parent: the parent node of this node in the PSyIR.
3427 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3428
3429 :raises GenerationError: if distributed memory is not enabled.
3430 :raises InternalError: if the supplied argument is not a scalar.
3431 :raises GenerationError: if the scalar is not of "real" intrinsic type.
3432
3433 '''
3434 def __init__(self, scalar, parent=None):
3435 # Check that distributed memory is enabled
3436 if not Config.get().distributed_memory:
3437 raise GenerationError(
3438 "It makes no sense to create a DynGlobalSum object when "
3439 "distributed memory is not enabled (dm=False).")
3440 # Check that the global sum argument is indeed a scalar
3441 if not scalar.is_scalar:
3442 raise InternalError(
3443 f"DynGlobalSum.init(): A global sum argument should be a "
3444 f"scalar but found argument of type '{scalar.argument_type}'.")
3445 # Check scalar intrinsic types that this class supports (only
3446 # "real" for now)
3447 if scalar.intrinsic_type != "real":
3448 raise GenerationError(
3449 f"DynGlobalSum currently only supports real scalars, but "
3450 f"argument '{scalar.name}' in Kernel '{scalar.call.name}' has "
3451 f"'{scalar.intrinsic_type}' intrinsic type.")
3452 # Initialise the parent class
3453 super().__init__(scalar, parent=parent)
3454
3455 def gen_code(self, parent):
3456 '''
3457 Dynamo-specific code generation for this class.
3458
3459 :param parent: f2pygen node to which to add AST nodes.
3460 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.SubroutineGen`
3461
3462 '''
3463 name = self._scalar.name
3464 # Use InvokeSchedule SymbolTable to share the same symbol for all
3465 # GlobalSums in the Invoke.
3466 sum_name = self.ancestor(InvokeSchedule).symbol_table.\
3467 find_or_create_tag("global_sum").name
3468 sum_type = self._scalar.data_type
3469 sum_mod = self._scalar.module_name
3470 parent.add(UseGen(parent, name=sum_mod, only=True,
3471 funcnames=[sum_type]))
3472 parent.add(TypeDeclGen(parent, datatype=sum_type,
3473 entity_decls=[sum_name]))
3474 parent.add(AssignGen(parent, lhs=sum_name+"%value", rhs=name))
3475 parent.add(AssignGen(parent, lhs=name, rhs=sum_name+"%get_sum()"))
3476
3477
3478def _create_depth_list(halo_info_list, parent):
3479 '''Halo exchanges may have more than one dependency. This method
3480 simplifies multiple dependencies to remove duplicates and any
3481 obvious redundancy. For example, if one dependency is for depth=1
3482 and another for depth=2 then we do not need the former as it is
3483 covered by the latter. Similarly, if we have a depth=extent+1 and
3484 another for depth=extent+2 then we do not need the former as it is
3485 covered by the latter. It also takes into account
3486 needs_clean_outer, which indicates whether the outermost halo
3487 needs to be clean (and therefore whether there is a dependence).
3488
3489 :param halo_info_list: a list containing halo access information
3490 derived from all read fields dependent on this halo exchange.
3491 :type: list[:py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloReadAccess`]
3492 :param parent: the parent PSyIR node of the related halo exchange.
3493 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3494
3495 :returns: a list containing halo depth information derived from
3496 the halo access information.
3497 :rtype: list[:py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloDepth]`
3498
3499 '''
3500 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
3501 depth_info_list = []
3502 # First look to see if all field dependencies are
3503 # annexed_only. If so we only care about annexed dofs.
3504 annexed_only = True
3505 for halo_info in halo_info_list:
3506 if not (halo_info.annexed_only or
3507 (halo_info.var_depth == Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE)
3508 and not halo_info.needs_clean_outer)):
3509 # There are two cases when we only care about accesses to
3510 # annexed dofs. 1) when annexed_only is set and 2) when
3511 # the halo depth is 1 but we only depend on annexed dofs
3512 # being up-to-date (needs_clean_outer is False).
3513 annexed_only = False
3514 break
3515 if annexed_only:
3516 depth_info = HaloDepth(parent)
3517 depth_info.set_by_value(max_depth=False,
3518 var_depth=Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE),
3519 annexed_only=True,
3520 max_depth_m1=False)
3521 return [depth_info]
3522 # Next look to see if one of the field dependencies specifies
3523 # a max_depth access. If so the whole halo region is accessed
3524 # so we do not need to be concerned with other accesses.
3525 max_depth_m1 = False
3526 for halo_info in halo_info_list:
3527 if halo_info.max_depth:
3528 if halo_info.needs_clean_outer:
3529 # Found a max_depth access so we only need one
3530 # HaloDepth entry.
3531 depth_info = HaloDepth(parent)
3532 depth_info.set_by_value(max_depth=True, var_depth=None,
3533 annexed_only=False, max_depth_m1=False)
3534 return [depth_info]
3535 # Remember that we found a max_depth-1 access.
3536 max_depth_m1 = True
3537
3538 if max_depth_m1:
3539 # We have at least one max_depth-1 access.
3540 depth_info = HaloDepth(parent)
3541 depth_info.set_by_value(max_depth=False, var_depth=None,
3542 annexed_only=False, max_depth_m1=True)
3543 depth_info_list.append(depth_info)
3544
3545 for halo_info in halo_info_list:
3546 # Go through the halo information associated with each
3547 # read dependency, skipping any max_depth-1 accesses.
3548 if halo_info.max_depth and not halo_info.needs_clean_outer:
3549 continue
3550 var_depth = halo_info.var_depth
3551 if var_depth and not halo_info.needs_clean_outer:
3552 # Decrease depth by 1 if we don't care about the outermost
3553 # access.
3554 var_depth = BinaryOperation.create(
3555 BinaryOperation.Operator.SUB,
3556 var_depth.copy(), Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE))
3557
3558 # check whether we match with existing depth information
3559 for depth_info in depth_info_list:
3560 if depth_info.var_depth == var_depth:
3561 # This dependence has exactly the same depth as an existing one
3562 # so no need to add a new HaloDepth.
3563 break
3564 else:
3565 # No matches were found with existing entries so create a
3566 # new one if 'var_depth' is set.
3567 if var_depth:
3568 depth_info = HaloDepth(parent)
3569 depth_info.set_by_value(max_depth=False, var_depth=var_depth,
3570 annexed_only=False, max_depth_m1=False)
3571 depth_info_list.append(depth_info)
3572 return depth_info_list
3573
3574
3575class LFRicHaloExchange(HaloExchange):
3576 '''LFRic-specific halo exchange class which can be added to and
3577 manipulated in a schedule.
3578
3579 :param field: the field that this halo exchange will act on
3580 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
3581 :param bool check_dirty: optional argument default True indicating
3582 whether this halo exchange should be subject to a run-time check
3583 for clean/dirty halos.
3584 :param vector_index: optional vector index (default None) to identify
3585 identify which index of a vector field this halo exchange is
3586 responsible for.
3587 :type vector_index: int
3588 :param parent: PSyIR parent node of this object.
3589 :type parent: Optional[:py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`]
3590
3591 '''
3592 def __init__(self, field, check_dirty=True,
3593 vector_index=None, parent=None):
3594 HaloExchange.__init__(self, field, check_dirty=check_dirty,
3595 vector_index=vector_index, parent=parent)
3596 # set up some defaults for this class
3597 self._halo_exchange_name = "halo_exchange"
3598
3599 def _compute_stencil_type(self):
3600 '''Dynamically work out the type of stencil required for this halo
3601 exchange as it could change as transformations are applied to
3602 the schedule. If all stencil accesses are of the same type then we
3603 return that stencil, otherwise we return the "region" stencil
3604 type (as it is safe for all stencils).
3605
3606 :return: the type of stencil required for this halo exchange
3607 :rtype: str
3608
3609 '''
3610 # get information about stencil accesses from all read fields
3611 # dependent on this halo exchange
3612 halo_info_list = self._compute_halo_read_info()
3613
3614 trial_stencil = halo_info_list[0].stencil_type
3615 for halo_info in halo_info_list:
3616 # assume that if stencil accesses are different that we
3617 # simply revert to region. We could be more clever in the
3618 # future e.g. x and y implies cross.
3619 if halo_info.stencil_type != trial_stencil:
3620 return "region"
3621 return trial_stencil
3622
3623 def _compute_halo_depth(self):
3624 '''Dynamically determine the depth of the halo for this halo exchange,
3625 as the depth can change as transformations are applied to the
3626 schedule.
3627
3628 :return: the PSyIR for the halo exchange depth.
3629 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3630
3631 '''
3632 depth_info_list = self._compute_halo_read_depth_info()
3633 if len(depth_info_list) == 1:
3634 psyir = depth_info_list[0].psyir_expression()
3635 else:
3636 psyir = IntrinsicCall.create(
3637 IntrinsicCall.Intrinsic.MAX,
3638 [depth.psyir_expression() for depth in depth_info_list])
3639
3640 # Simplify the resulting expression. We need to create a fake
3641 # Assignment to temporarily host the expression.
3642 sym_maths = SymbolicMaths.get()
3643 fake_assign = Assignment.create(
3644 Reference(DataSymbol("tmp", INTEGER_TYPE)), psyir)
3645 self.parentparent.addchild(fake_assign)
3646
3647 sym_maths.expand(fake_assign.rhs)
3648 depth_expr = fake_assign.rhs.detach()
3649 fake_assign.detach()
3650 return depth_expr
3651
3652 def _compute_halo_read_depth_info(self, ignore_hex_dep=False):
3653 '''Take a list of `psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloReadAccess` objects and
3654 create an equivalent list of `psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloDepth`
3655 objects. Whilst doing this we simplify the
3656 `psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloDepth` list to remove redundant depth
3657 information e.g. depth=1 is not required if we have a depth=2.
3658 If the optional ignore_hex_dep argument is set to True then
3659 any read accesses contained in halo exchange nodes are
3660 ignored. This option can therefore be used to filter out any
3661 halo exchange dependencies and only return non-halo exchange
3662 dependencies if and when required.
3663
3664 :param bool ignore_hex_dep: if True then ignore any read \
3665 accesses contained in halo exchanges. This is an optional \
3666 argument that defaults to False.
3667
3668 :return: a list containing halo depth information derived from \
3669 all fields dependent on this halo exchange.
3670 :rtype: :func:`list` of :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloDepth`
3671
3672 '''
3673 # get our halo information
3674 halo_info_list = self._compute_halo_read_info(ignore_hex_dep)
3675 # use the halo information to generate depth information
3676 depth_info_list = _create_depth_list(halo_info_list, self)
3677 return depth_info_list
3678
3679 def _compute_halo_read_info(self, ignore_hex_dep=False):
3680 '''Dynamically computes all halo read dependencies and returns the
3681 required halo information (i.e. halo depth and stencil type)
3682 in a list of HaloReadAccess objects. If the optional
3683 ignore_hex_dep argument is set to True then any read accesses
3684 contained in halo exchange nodes are ignored. This option can
3685 therefore be used to filter out any halo exchange dependencies
3686 and only return non-halo exchange dependencies if and when
3687 required.
3688
3689 :param bool ignore_hex_dep: if True then ignore any read \
3690 accesses contained in halo exchanges. This is an optional \
3691 argument that defaults to False.
3692
3693 :return: a list containing halo information for each read dependency.
3694 :rtype: :func:`list` of :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloReadAccess`
3695
3696 :raises InternalError: if there is more than one read \
3697 dependency associated with a halo exchange.
3698 :raises InternalError: if there is a read dependency \
3699 associated with a halo exchange and it is not the last \
3700 entry in the read dependency list.
3701 :raises GenerationError: if there is a read dependency \
3702 associated with an asynchronous halo exchange.
3703 :raises InternalError: if no read dependencies are found.
3704
3705 '''
3706 read_dependencies = self.field.forward_read_dependencies()
3707 hex_deps = [dep for dep in read_dependencies
3708 if isinstance(dep.call, LFRicHaloExchange)]
3709 if hex_deps:
3710 # There is a field accessed by a halo exchange that is
3711 # a read dependence. As ignore_hex_dep is True this should
3712 # be ignored so this is removed from the list.
3713 if any(dep for dep in hex_deps
3714 if isinstance(dep.call, (LFRicHaloExchangeStart,
3715 LFRicHaloExchangeEnd))):
3716 raise GenerationError(
3717 "Please perform redundant computation transformations "
3718 "before asynchronous halo exchange transformations.")
3719
3720 # There can only be one field accessed by a
3721 # halo exchange that is a read dependence.
3722 if len(hex_deps) != 1:
3723 raise InternalError(
3724 f"There should only ever be at most one read dependency "
3725 f"associated with a halo exchange in the read dependency "
3726 f"list, but found {len(hex_deps)} for field "
3727 f"{self.field.name}.")
3728 # For sanity, check that the field accessed by the halo
3729 # exchange is the last dependence in the list.
3730 if not isinstance(read_dependencies[-1].call, LFRicHaloExchange):
3731 raise InternalError(
3732 "If there is a read dependency associated with a halo "
3733 "exchange in the list of read dependencies then it should "
3734 "be the last one in the list.")
3735 if ignore_hex_dep:
3736 # Remove the last entry in the list (the field accessed by
3737 # the halo exchange).
3738 del read_dependencies[-1]
3739
3740 if not read_dependencies:
3741 raise InternalError(
3742 "Internal logic error. There should be at least one read "
3743 "dependence for a halo exchange.")
3744 return [HaloReadAccess(read_dependency, self._symbol_table_symbol_table) for
3745 read_dependency in read_dependencies]
3746
3747 def _compute_halo_write_info(self):
3748 '''Determines how much of the halo has been cleaned from any previous
3749 redundant computation.
3750
3751 :return: a HaloWriteAccess object containing the required
3752 information, or None if no dependence information is found.
3753 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.HaloWriteAccess` | None
3754
3755 :raises GenerationError: if more than one write dependence is
3756 found for this halo exchange as this should not be possible.
3757
3758 '''
3759 write_dependencies = self.field.backward_write_dependencies()
3760 if not write_dependencies:
3761 # no write dependence information
3762 return None
3763 if len(write_dependencies) > 1:
3764 raise GenerationError(
3765 f"Internal logic error. There should be at most one write "
3766 f"dependence for a halo exchange. Found "
3767 f"'{len(write_dependencies)}'")
3768 return HaloWriteAccess(write_dependencies[0], parent=self)
3769
3770 def required(self, ignore_hex_dep=False):
3771 '''Determines whether this halo exchange is definitely required
3772 ``(True, True)``, might be required ``(True, False)`` or is definitely
3773 not required ``(False, *)``.
3774
3775 If the optional ignore_hex_dep argument is set to True then
3776 any read accesses contained in halo exchange nodes are
3777 ignored. This option can therefore be used to filter out any
3778 halo exchange dependencies and only consider non-halo exchange
3779 dependencies if and when required.
3780
3781 Whilst a halo exchange is generally only ever added if it is
3782 required, or if it may be required, this situation can change
3783 if redundant computation transformations are applied. The
3784 first argument can be used to remove such halo exchanges if
3785 required.
3786
3787 When the first return value is True, the second return value
3788 can be used to see if we need to rely on the runtime
3789 (set_dirty and set_clean calls) and therefore add a
3790 check_dirty() call around the halo exchange or whether we
3791 definitely know that this halo exchange is required.
3792
3793 This routine assumes that a stencil size provided via a
3794 variable may take the value 0. If a variables value is
3795 constrained to be 1, or more, then the logic for deciding
3796 whether a halo exchange is definitely required should be
3797 updated. Note, the routine would still be correct as is, it
3798 would just return more unknown results than it should).
3799
3800 :param bool ignore_hex_dep: if True then ignore any read \
3801 accesses contained in halo exchanges. This is an optional \
3802 argument that defaults to False.
3803
3804 :returns: (x, y) where x specifies whether this halo
3805 exchange is (or might be) required - True, or is not
3806 required - False. If the first tuple item is True then the
3807 second argument specifies whether we definitely know that
3808 we need the HaloExchange - True, or are not sure - False.
3809 :rtype: (bool, bool)
3810
3811 '''
3812 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches, too-many-return-statements
3813 # get *aggregated* information about halo reads
3814 required_clean_info = self._compute_halo_read_depth_info(
3815 ignore_hex_dep)
3816 # get information about the halo write
3817 clean_info = self._compute_halo_write_info()
3818
3819 # no need to test whether we return at least one read
3820 # dependency as _compute_halo_read_depth_info() raises an
3821 # exception if none are found
3822
3823 if (Config.get().api_conf("lfric").compute_annexed_dofs and
3824 len(required_clean_info) == 1 and
3825 required_clean_info[0].annexed_only):
3826 # We definitely don't need the halo exchange as we
3827 # only read annexed dofs and these are always clean as
3828 # they are computed by default when iterating over
3829 # dofs and kept up-to-date by redundant computation
3830 # when iterating over cells.
3831 required = False
3832 known = True # redundant information as it is always known
3833 return required, known
3834
3835 if not clean_info:
3836 # this halo exchange has no previous write dependencies so
3837 # we do not know the initial state of the halo. This means
3838 # that we do not know if we need a halo exchange or not
3839 required = True
3840 known = False
3841 return required, known
3842
3843 if clean_info.max_depth:
3844 if not clean_info.dirty_outer:
3845 # all of the halo is cleaned by redundant computation
3846 # so halo exchange is not required
3847 required = False
3848 known = True # redundant information as it is always known
3849 else:
3850 # the last level halo is dirty
3851 if required_clean_info[0].max_depth:
3852 # we know that we need to clean the outermost halo level
3853 required = True
3854 known = True
3855 else:
3856 # we don't know whether the halo exchange is
3857 # required or not as the reader reads the halo to
3858 # a specified depth but we don't know the depth
3859 # of the halo
3860 required = True
3861 known = False
3862 return required, known
3863
3864 # At this point we know that clean_info.max_depth is False
3865 clean_depth = clean_info.clean_depth
3866
3867 if not clean_depth:
3868 if clean_info.dirty_outer:
3869 # the writer redundantly computes in the level 1 halo but
3870 # leaves it dirty (although annexed dofs are now clean).
3871 if len(required_clean_info) == 1 and \
3872 required_clean_info[0].annexed_only:
3873 # we definitely don't need the halo exchange as we
3874 # only read annexed dofs and these have been made
3875 # clean by the redundant computation
3876 required = False
3877 known = True # redundant information as it is always known
3878 else:
3879 # we definitely need the halo exchange as the reader(s)
3880 # require the halo to be clean
3881 required = True
3882 known = True
3883 return required, known
3884 else:
3885 # if clean_depth is 0 then the writer does not
3886 # redundantly compute so we definitely need the halo
3887 # exchange
3888 required = True
3889 known = True
3890 return required, known
3891
3892 # We have a clean_depth so iterate over the various required depths
3893 # to see whether or not they are all satisfied.
3894 required = False
3895 known = False
3896 for required_clean in required_clean_info:
3897 if required_clean.max_depth or required_clean.max_depth_m1:
3898 required = True
3899 known = False
3900 return required, known
3901 left_dirty = SymbolicMaths.greater_than(
3902 required_clean.var_depth, clean_depth,
3903 all_variables_positive=True)
3904 if left_dirty == SymbolicMaths.Fuzzy.FALSE:
3905 # Nothing is left dirty so no hexch required for this
3906 # read access.
3907 continue
3908 if left_dirty == SymbolicMaths.Fuzzy.TRUE:
3909 # Halo definitely left dirty to a certain depth.
3910 required = True
3911 known = True
3912 return required, known
3913 # Otherwise, we can't be sure. Continue looking at the other
3914 # read accesses in case one of them is definitely not satisfied.
3915 required = True
3916 continue
3917
3918 # If we get to here then we may or may not require a halo exchange.
3919 # If we do need one, then we aren't certain about it (as we'd already
3920 # have returned if we were).
3921 if not required:
3922 # We know we don't require a halo exchange.
3923 known = True
3924
3925 return required, known
3926
3927 def node_str(self, colour=True):
3928 ''' Creates a text summary of this HaloExchange node.
3929
3930 :param bool colour: whether or not to include control codes for colour.
3931
3932 :returns: text summary of this node, optionally with control codes \
3933 for colour highlighting.
3934 :rtype: str
3935
3936 '''
3937 _, known = self.required()
3938 runtime_check = not known
3939 field_id = self._field.name
3940 if self.vector_indexvector_indexvector_index:
3941 field_id += f"({self.vector_index})"
3942 return (f"{self.coloured_name(colour)}[field='{field_id}', "
3943 f"type='{self._compute_stencil_type()}', "
3944 f"depth={self._compute_halo_depth().debug_string()}, "
3945 f"check_dirty={runtime_check}]")
3946
3947 def gen_code(self, parent):
3948 '''Dynamo specific code generation for this class.
3949
3950 :param parent: an f2pygen object that will be the parent of \
3951 f2pygen objects created in this method
3952 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.f2pygen.BaseGen`
3953
3954 '''
3955 parent.add(PSyIRGen(parent, self))
3956
3957 def lower_to_language_level(self):
3958 '''
3959 :returns: this node lowered to language-level PSyIR.
3960 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
3961 '''
3962 symbol = DataSymbol(self._field.proxy_name, UnresolvedType())
3963 method = self._halo_exchange_name
3964 depth_expr = self._compute_halo_depth()
3965
3966 # Create infrastructure Calls
3967 if self.vector_indexvector_indexvector_index:
3968 idx = Literal(str(self.vector_indexvector_indexvector_index), INTEGER_TYPE)
3969 if_condition = Call.create(
3970 ArrayOfStructuresReference.create(symbol, [idx], ['is_dirty']),
3971 [('depth', depth_expr.copy())])
3972 if_body = Call.create(
3973 ArrayOfStructuresReference.create(
3974 symbol, [idx.copy()], [method]),
3975 [('depth', depth_expr.copy())])
3976 else:
3977 if_condition = Call.create(
3978 StructureReference.create(symbol, ['is_dirty']),
3979 [('depth', depth_expr.copy())])
3980 if_body = Call.create(
3981 StructureReference.create(symbol, [method]),
3982 [('depth', depth_expr.copy())])
3983
3984 # Add the "if_dirty" check when necessary
3985 _, known = self.required()
3986 if not known:
3987 haloex = IfBlock.create(if_condition, [if_body])
3988 else:
3989 haloex = if_body
3990
3991 self.replace_with(haloex)
3992 return haloex
3993
3994
3995class LFRicHaloExchangeStart(LFRicHaloExchange):
3996 '''The start of an asynchronous halo exchange. This is similar to a
3997 regular halo exchange except that the Fortran name of the call is
3998 different and the routine only reads the data being transferred
3999 (the associated field is specified as having a read access). As a
4000 result this class is not able to determine some important
4001 properties (such as whether the halo exchange is known to be
4002 required or not). This is solved by finding the corresponding
4003 asynchronous halo exchange end (a halo exchange start always has a
4004 corresponding halo exchange end and vice versa) and calling its
4005 methods (a halo exchange end is specified as having readwrite
4006 access to its associated field and therefore is able to determine
4007 the required properties).
4008
4009 :param field: the field that this halo exchange will act on
4010 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
4011 :param check_dirty: optional argument (default True) indicating \
4012 whether this halo exchange should be subject to a run-time check \
4013 for clean/dirty halos.
4014 :type check_dirty: bool
4015 :param vector_index: optional vector index (default None) to \
4016 identify which component of a vector field this halo exchange is \
4017 responsible for
4018 :type vector_index: int
4019 :param parent: optional PSyIRe parent node (default None) of this \
4020 object
4021 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4022
4023 '''
4024 # Textual description of the node.
4025 _text_name = "HaloExchangeStart"
4026 _colour = "yellow"
4027
4028 def __init__(self, field, check_dirty=True,
4029 vector_index=None, parent=None):
4030 LFRicHaloExchange.__init__(self, field, check_dirty=check_dirty,
4031 vector_index=vector_index, parent=parent)
4032 # Update the field's access appropriately. Here "gh_read"
4033 # specifies that the start of a halo exchange only reads
4034 # the field's data.
4035 self._field.access = AccessType.READ
4036 # override appropriate parent class names
4037 self._halo_exchange_name_halo_exchange_name = "halo_exchange_start"
4038
4039 def _compute_stencil_type(self):
4040 '''Call the required method in the corresponding halo exchange end
4041 object. This is done as the field in halo exchange start is
4042 only read and the dependence analysis beneath this call
4043 requires the field to be modified.
4044
4045 :return: Return the type of stencil required for this pair of \
4046 halo exchanges
4047 :rtype: str
4048
4049 '''
4050 # pylint: disable=protected-access
4051 return self._get_hex_end()._compute_stencil_type()
4052
4053 def _compute_halo_depth(self):
4054 '''Call the required method in the corresponding halo exchange end
4055 object. This is done as the field in halo exchange start is
4056 only read and the dependence analysis beneath this call
4057 requires the field to be modified.
4058
4059 :return: Return the halo exchange depth as a Fortran string
4060 :rtype: str
4061
4062 '''
4063 # pylint: disable=protected-access
4064 return self._get_hex_end()._compute_halo_depth()
4065
4066 def required(self):
4067 '''Call the required method in the corresponding halo exchange end
4068 object. This is done as the field in halo exchange start is
4069 only read and the dependence analysis beneath this call
4070 requires the field to be modified.
4071
4072 :returns: (x, y) where x specifies whether this halo exchange \
4073 is (or might be) required - True, or is not required \
4074 - False. If the first tuple item is True then the second \
4075 argument specifies whether we definitely know that we need \
4076 the HaloExchange - True, or are not sure - False.
4077 :rtype: (bool, bool)
4078
4079 '''
4080 return self._get_hex_end().required()
4081
4082 def _get_hex_end(self):
4083 '''An internal helper routine for this class which finds the halo
4084 exchange end object corresponding to this halo exchange start
4085 object or raises an exception if one is not found.
4086
4087 :return: The corresponding halo exchange end object
4088 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.LFRicHaloExchangeEnd`
4089 :raises GenerationError: If no matching HaloExchangeEnd is \
4090 found, or if the first matching haloexchange that is found is \
4091 not a HaloExchangeEnd
4092
4093 '''
4094 # Look at all nodes following this one in schedule order
4095 # (which is PSyIRe node order)
4096 for node in self.following():
4097 if self.sameParent(node) and isinstance(node, LFRicHaloExchange):
4098 # Found a following `haloexchange`,
4099 # `haloexchangestart` or `haloexchangeend` PSyIRe node
4100 # that is at the same calling hierarchy level as this
4101 # haloexchangestart
4102 access = DataAccess(self.field)
4103 if access.overlaps(node.field):
4104 if isinstance(node, LFRicHaloExchangeEnd):
4105 return node
4106 raise GenerationError(
4107 f"Halo exchange start for field '{self.field.name}' "
4108 f"should match with a halo exchange end, but found "
4109 f"{type(node)}")
4110 # no match has been found which is an error as a halo exchange
4111 # start should always have a matching halo exchange end that
4112 # follows it in schedule (PSyIRe sibling) order
4113 raise GenerationError(
4114 f"Halo exchange start for field '{self.field.name}' has no "
4115 f"matching halo exchange end")
4116
4117
4118class LFRicHaloExchangeEnd(LFRicHaloExchange):
4119 '''The end of an asynchronous halo exchange. This is similar to a
4120 regular halo exchange except that the Fortran name of the call is
4121 different and the routine only writes to the data being
4122 transferred.
4123
4124 :param field: the field that this halo exchange will act on
4125 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
4126 :param check_dirty: optional argument (default True) indicating \
4127 whether this halo exchange should be subject to a run-time check \

4130 :param vector_index: optional vector index (default None) to \

4134 :param parent: optional PSyIRe parent node (default None) of this \
4135 object
4136 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4137
4138 '''
4139 # Textual description of the node.
4140 _text_name = "HaloExchangeEnd"
4141 _colour = "yellow"

4144 vector_index=None, parent=None):

4146 vector_index=vector_index, parent=parent)
4147 # Update field properties appropriately. The associated field is
4148 # written to. However, a readwrite field access needs to be
4149 # specified as this is required for the halo exchange logic to

4151 self._field.access = AccessType.READWRITE
4152 # override appropriate parent class names
