4156class HaloDepth():
4157 '''Determines how much of the halo a read to a field accesses (the
4158 halo depth).
4159
4160 :param parent: the parent PSyIR node of the region containing the field
4161 access that is represented.
4162 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4163
4164 '''
4165 def __init__(self, parent):
4166 # var_depth is used to store the PSyIR of the expression holding
4167 # depth of halo that is accessed.
4168 self._var_depth = None
4169 # max_depth specifies whether the full depth of halo (whatever
4170 # that might be) is accessed. If this is set then
4171 # literal_depth, var_depth and max_depth_m1 have no
4172 # meaning. max_depth being False does not necessarily mean the
4173 # full halo depth is not accessed, rather it means that we do
4174 # not know.
4175 self._max_depth = False
4176 # max_depth_m1 specifies whether the full depth of halo
4177 # (whatever that might be) apart from the outermost level is
4178 # accessed. If this is set then literal_depth, var_depth and
4179 # max_depth have no meaning.
4180 self._max_depth_m1 = False
4181 # annexed only is True if the only access in the halo is for
4182 # annexed dofs
4183 self._annexed_only = False
4184 # Keep a reference to the symbol table so that we can look-up
4185 # variables holding the maximum halo depth.
4186 # TODO #2503: This can become invalid if the HaloExchange
4187 # containing this HaloDepth changes its ancestors.
4188 self._parent = parent
4189
4190 @property
4191 def annexed_only(self):
4192 '''
4193 :returns: True if only annexed dofs are accessed in the halo and
4194 False otherwise.
4195 :rtype: bool
4196 '''
4197 return self._annexed_only
4198
4199 @property
4200 def max_depth(self):
4201 '''
4202 :returns: True if the read to the field is known to access all
4203 of the halo and False otherwise.
4204 :rtype: bool
4205 '''
4206 return self._max_depth
4207
4208 @property
4209 def max_depth_m1(self):
4210 '''Returns whether the read to the field is known to access all of the
4211 halo except the outermost level or not.
4212
4213 :returns: True if the read to the field is known to access all
4214 of the halo except the outermost and False otherwise.
4215 :rtype: bool
4216
4217 '''
4218 return self._max_depth_m1
4219
4220 @property
4221 def var_depth(self):
4222 '''Returns the PSyIR of the expression specifying the depth of halo
4223 access if one is provided.
4224
4225 :returns: PSyIR specifying the halo access depth
4226 if one exists, and None if not.
4227 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Statement`
4228
4229 '''
4230 return self._var_depth
4231
4232 def set_by_value(self, max_depth, var_depth, annexed_only, max_depth_m1):
4233 # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
4234 '''Set halo depth information directly
4235
4236 :param bool max_depth: True if the field accesses all of the
4237 halo and False otherwise
4238 :param var_depth: PSyIR expression specifying the halo
4239 access depth, if one exists, and None if not
4240 :type var_depth: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4241 :param bool annexed_only: True if only the halo's annexed dofs
4242 are accessed and False otherwise
4243 :param bool max_depth_m1: True if the field accesses all of
4244 the halo but does not require the outermost halo to be correct
4245 and False otherwise
4246
4247 '''
4248 self._max_depth = max_depth
4249 self._annexed_only = annexed_only
4250 self._max_depth_m1 = max_depth_m1
4251 self._var_depth = None
4252
4253 if not var_depth:
4254 return
4255
4256 # Simplify any provided PSyIR expression.
4257 sym_maths = SymbolicMaths.get()
4258 # In order to be able to apply the SymbolicMaths.expand() method we
4259 # have to create a fake Assignment and temporarily graft it into the
4260 # tree.
4261 fake_assign = Assignment.create(
4262 Reference(DataSymbol("tmp", INTEGER_TYPE)), var_depth.detach())
4263 sched = self._parent.ancestor(Schedule, include_self=True)
4264 sched.addchild(fake_assign)
4265
4266 sym_maths.expand(fake_assign.rhs)
4267 self._var_depth = fake_assign.rhs.detach()
4268 fake_assign.detach()
4269
4270 def psyir_expression(self):
4271 '''
4272 :returns: the PSyIR expression representing this HaloDepth.
4273 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4274 '''
4275 table = self._parent.scope.symbol_table
4276 if self.max_depthmax_depth:
4277 max_depth = table.lookup_with_tag("max_halo_depth_mesh")
4278 return Reference(max_depth)
4279 if self.max_depth_m1max_depth_m1:
4280 max_depth = table.lookup_with_tag("max_halo_depth_mesh")
4281 return BinaryOperation.create(
4282 BinaryOperation.Operator.SUB,
4283 Reference(max_depth),
4284 Literal('1', INTEGER_TYPE))
4285 if self.var_depthvar_depth:
4286 return self.var_depthvar_depth.copy()
4287
4288 return None
4289
4290
4291def halo_check_arg(field, access_types):
4292 '''
4293 Support function which performs checks to ensure the first argument
4294 is a field, that the field is contained within Kernel or Builtin
4295 call and that the field is accessed in one of the ways specified
4296 by the second argument. If no error is reported it returns the
4297 call object containing this argument.
4298
4299 :param field: the argument object we are checking
4300 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynArgument`
4301 :param access_types: List of allowed access types.
4302 :type access_types: List of :py:class:`psyclone.psyGen.AccessType`.
4303 :return: the call containing the argument object
4304 :rtype: sub-class of :py:class:`psyclone.psyGen.Kern`
4305
4306 :raises GenerationError: if the first argument to this function is \
4307 the wrong type.
4308 :raises GenerationError: if the first argument is not accessed in one of \
4309 the ways specified by the second argument to the function.
4310 :raises GenerationError: if the first argument is not contained \
4311 within a call object.
4312
4313 '''
4314 try:
4315 # Get the kernel/built-in call associated with this field
4316 call = field.call
4317 except AttributeError as err:
4318 raise GenerationError(
4319 f"HaloInfo class expects an argument of type DynArgument, or "
4320 f"equivalent, on initialisation, but found, "
4321 f"'{type(field)}'") from err
4322
4323 if field.access not in access_types:
4324 api_strings = [access.api_specific_name() for access in access_types]
4325 raise GenerationError(
4326 f"In HaloInfo class, field '{field.name}' should be one of "
4327 f"{api_strings}, but found '{field.access.api_specific_name()}'")
4328 if not isinstance(call, (LFRicBuiltIn, LFRicKern)):
4329 raise GenerationError(
4330 f"In HaloInfo class, field '{field.name}' should be from a call "
4331 f"but found {type(call)}")
4332 return call
4333
4334
4335class HaloWriteAccess(HaloDepth):
4336 '''Determines how much of a field's halo is written to (the halo depth)
4337 when a field is accessed in a particular kernel within a
4338 particular loop nest.
4339
4340 :param field: the field that we are concerned with.
4341 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynArgument`
4342 :param parent: the parent PSyIR node associated with the scoping region
4343 that contains this halo access.
4344 :type parent: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
4345
4346 '''
4347 def __init__(self, field, parent):
4348 HaloDepth.__init__(self, parent)
4349 self._compute_from_field(field)
4350
4351 @property
4352 def dirty_outer(self):
4353 '''Returns True if the writer is continuous and accesses the halo and
4354 False otherwise. It indicates that the outer level of halo that has
4355 been written to is actually dirty (well to be precise it is a partial
4356 sum).
4357
4358 :returns: True if the outer layer of halo that is written \
4359 to remains dirty and False otherwise.
4360 :rtype: bool
4361
4362 '''
4363 return self._dirty_outer
4364
4365 @property
4366 def clean_depth(self):
4367 '''
4368 Returns the depth to which this halo is clean following the write.
4369
4370 :returns: PSyIR for the expression for the clean halo depth or None.
4371 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node` | NoneType
4372
4373 '''
4374 if self.var_depthvar_depthvar_depth:
4375 halo_depth = self.var_depthvar_depthvar_depth
4376 elif self.max_depthmax_depthmax_depth:
4377 # halo accesses(s) is/are to the full halo
4378 # depth (-1 if continuous)
4379 table = self._parent.scope.symbol_table
4380 halo_depth = Reference(
4381 table.lookup_with_tag("max_halo_depth_mesh"))
4382 else:
4383 return None
4384
4385 if self.dirty_outerdirty_outer:
4386 halo_depth = BinaryOperation.create(
4387 BinaryOperation.Operator.SUB,
4388 halo_depth.copy(), Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE))
4389
4390 sym_maths = SymbolicMaths.get()
4391 fake_assign = Assignment.create(
4392 Reference(DataSymbol("tmp", INTEGER_TYPE)),
4393 halo_depth)
4394 sched = self._parent.ancestor(Schedule)
4395 sched.addchild(fake_assign)
4396
4397 sym_maths.expand(fake_assign.rhs)
4398 depth_expr = fake_assign.rhs.detach()
4399 fake_assign.detach()
4400 if depth_expr == Literal("0", INTEGER_TYPE):
4401 return None
4402 return depth_expr
4403
4404 def _compute_from_field(self, field):
4405 '''Internal method to compute what parts of a field's halo are written
4406 to in a certain kernel and loop. The information computed is the depth
4407 of access and validity of the data after writing. The depth of access
4408 can be the maximum halo depth or a specified (literal or variable)
4409 depth and the outer halo layer that is written to may be dirty or
4410 clean.
4411
4412 :param field: the field that we are concerned with.
4413 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynArgument`
4414
4415 '''
4416 const = LFRicConstants()
4417
4418 call = halo_check_arg(field, AccessType.all_write_accesses())
4419 # no test required here as all calls exist within a loop
4420
4421 loop = call.parent.parent
4422 # The outermost halo level that is written to is dirty if it
4423 # is a continuous field which writes into the halo in a loop
4424 # over cells
4425 self._dirty_outer = (
4426 not field.discontinuous and
4427 loop.iteration_space.endswith("cell_column") and
4428 loop.upper_bound_name in const.HALO_ACCESS_LOOP_BOUNDS)
4429 depth = None
4430 max_depth = False
4431 if loop.upper_bound_name in const.HALO_ACCESS_LOOP_BOUNDS:
4432 # loop does redundant computation
4433 if loop.upper_bound_halo_depth:
4434 # loop redundant computation is to a certain depth.
4435 depth = loop.upper_bound_halo_depth
4436 else:
4437 # loop redundant computation is to the maximum depth
4438 max_depth = True
4439 # If this is an inter-grid kernel and we're writing to the
4440 # field on the fine mesh then the halo depth is effectively
4441 # doubled
4442 if call.is_intergrid and field.mesh == "gh_fine" and depth:
4443 depth = BinaryOperation.create(
4444 BinaryOperation.Operator.MUL,
4445 Literal("2", INTEGER_TYPE), depth.copy())
4446 # The third argument for set_by_value gives the PSyIR of the
4447 # expression specifying the depth.
4448 var_depth = depth
4449 # The fourth argument for set_by_value indicates whether
4450 # we only access annexed_dofs. At the moment this is not possible when
4451 # modifying a field so we always supply False. The fifth
4452 # argument indicates if the depth of access is the
4453 # maximum-1. This is not possible here so we supply False.
4454 HaloDepth.set_by_value(self, max_depth, var_depth,
4455 False, False)
4456
4457
4458class HaloReadAccess(HaloDepth):
4459 '''Determines how much of a field's halo is read (the halo depth) and
4460 additionally the access pattern (the stencil) when a field is
4461 accessed in a particular kernel within a particular loop nest.
4462
4463 :param field: the field for which we want information.
4464 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
4465 :param sym_table: the symbol table associated with the scoping region
4466 that contains this halo access.
4467 :type sym_table: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.SymbolTable`
4468
4469 '''
4470 def __init__(self, field, parent=None):
4471 super().__init__(parent)
4472 self._stencil_type = None
4473 self._needs_clean_outer = None
4474 self._compute_from_field(field)
4475
4476 @property
4477 def needs_clean_outer(self):
4478 '''Returns False if the reader has a gh_inc access and accesses the
4479 halo. Otherwise returns True. Indicates that the outer level
4480 of halo that has been read does not need to be clean (although
4481 any annexed dofs do).
4482
4483 :return: Returns False if the outer layer of halo that is read \
4484 does not need to be clean and True otherwise.
4485 :rtype: bool
4486
4487 '''
4488 return self._needs_clean_outer
4489
4490 @property
4491 def stencil_type(self):
4492 '''Returns the type of stencil access used by the field(s) in the halo
4493 if one exists. If redundant computation (accessing the full
4494 halo) is combined with a stencil access (potentially accessing
4495 a subset of the halo) then the access is assumed to be full
4496 access (region) for all depths.
4497
4498 :returns: the type of stencil access used or None if there is no \
4499 stencil.
4500 :rtype: str
4501
4502 '''
4503 return self._stencil_type
4504
4505 def _compute_from_field(self, field):
4506 '''Internal method to compute which parts of a field's halo are read
4507 in a certain kernel and loop. The information computed is the
4508 depth of access and the access pattern. The depth of access
4509 can be the maximum halo depth or a PSyIR expression specifying the
4510 depth. The access pattern will only be specified if the kernel code
4511 performs a stencil access on the field.
4512
4513 :param field: the field that we are concerned with
4514 :type field: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynArgument`
4515
4516 '''
4517 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
4518 const = LFRicConstants()
4519
4520 self._annexed_only_annexed_only = False
4521 call = halo_check_arg(field, AccessType.all_read_accesses())
4522
4523 loop = call.ancestor(LFRicLoop)
4524 table = loop.ancestor(InvokeSchedule).symbol_table
4525
4526 # For GH_INC we accumulate contributions into the field being
4527 # modified. In order to get correct results for owned and
4528 # annexed dofs, this requires that the fields we are
4529 # accumulating contributions from have up-to-date values in
4530 # the halo cell(s). However, we do not need to be concerned
4531 # with the values of the modified field in the last-level of
4532 # the halo. This is because we only have enough information to
4533 # partially compute the contributions in those cells
4534 # anyway. (If the values of the field being modified are
4535 # required, at some later point, in that level of the halo
4536 # then we do a halo swap.)
4537 self._needs_clean_outer = (
4538 not (field.access == AccessType.INC
4539 and loop.upper_bound_name in ["cell_halo",
4540 "colour_halo"]))
4541 # now we have the parent loop we can work out what part of the
4542 # halo this field accesses
4543 if loop.upper_bound_name in const.HALO_ACCESS_LOOP_BOUNDS:
4544 # this loop performs redundant computation
4545 if loop.upper_bound_halo_depth:
4546 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = loop.upper_bound_halo_depth
4547 else:
4548 # loop redundant computation is to the maximum depth
4549 self._max_depth_max_depth = True
4550 elif loop.upper_bound_name == "ncolour":
4551 # Loop is coloured but does not access the halo.
4552 pass
4553 elif loop.upper_bound_name in ["ncells", "nannexed"]:
4554 if field.descriptor.stencil:
4555 # no need to worry about annexed dofs (if they exist)
4556 # as the stencil will cover these (this is currently
4557 # guaranteed as halo exchanges only exchange full
4558 # halos)
4559 pass
4560 else: # there is no stencil
4561 if (field.discontinuous or call.iterates_over == "dof" or
4562 call.all_updates_are_writes):
4563 # There are only local accesses or the kernel is of the
4564 # special form where any iteration is guaranteed to write
4565 # the same value to a given shared entity.
4566 pass
4567 else:
4568 # This is a continuous field which therefore
4569 # accesses annexed dofs. We set access to the
4570 # level 1 halo here as there is currently no
4571 # mechanism to perform a halo exchange solely on
4572 # annexed dofs.
4573 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = Literal("1", INTEGER_TYPE)
4574 self._annexed_only_annexed_only = True
4575 elif loop.upper_bound_name == "ndofs":
4576 # we only access owned dofs so there is no access to the
4577 # halo
4578 pass
4579 else:
4580 raise GenerationError(
4581 f"Internal error in HaloReadAccess._compute_from_field. Found "
4582 f"unexpected loop upper bound name '{loop.upper_bound_name}'")
4583
4584 if self._max_depth_max_depth or self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth:
4585 # Whilst stencil type has no real meaning when there is no
4586 # stencil it is convenient to set it to "region" when
4587 # there is redundant computation as the halo exchange
4588 # logic is interested in the access pattern irrespective
4589 # of whether there is a stencil access or not. We use
4590 # "region" as it means access all of the halo data which
4591 # is what is done when performing redundant computation
4592 # with no stencil.
4593 self._stencil_type = "region"
4594 if field.descriptor.stencil:
4595 # field has a stencil access
4596 if self._max_depth_max_depth:
4597 raise GenerationError(
4598 "redundant computation to max depth with a stencil is "
4599 "invalid")
4600 self._stencil_type = field.descriptor.stencil['type']
4601 if self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth:
4602 # halo exchange does not support mixed accesses to the halo
4603 # so we simply set the stencil type as 'region'.
4604 self._stencil_type = "region"
4605 stencil_depth = field.descriptor.stencil['extent']
4606 if stencil_depth:
4607 # stencil_depth is provided in the kernel metadata
4608 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = BinaryOperation.create(
4609 BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD,
4610 Literal(str(stencil_depth), INTEGER_TYPE),
4611 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth.copy())
4612 else:
4613 # Stencil_depth is provided by the algorithm layer.
4614 # It is currently not possible to specify kind for an
4615 # integer literal stencil depth in a kernel call. This
4616 # will be enabled when addressing issue #753.
4617 if field.stencil.extent_arg.is_literal():
4618 # a literal is specified
4619 value_str = field.stencil.extent_arg.text
4620 stencil_depth = Literal(value_str, INTEGER_TYPE)
4621 else:
4622 # a variable is specified
4623 stencil_depth = Reference(
4624 table.lookup(field.stencil.extent_arg.varname))
4625 if self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth:
4626 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = BinaryOperation.create(
4627 BinaryOperation.Operator.ADD,
4628 stencil_depth, self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth.copy())
4629 else:
4630 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = stencil_depth
4631 # If this is an intergrid kernel and the field in question is on
4632 # the fine mesh then we must double the halo depth
4633 if call.is_intergrid and field.mesh == "gh_fine":
4634 if self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth:
4635 self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth = BinaryOperation.create(
4636 BinaryOperation.Operator.MUL,
4637 Literal("2", INTEGER_TYPE), self._var_depth_var_depth_var_depth.copy())
4638
4639
4640class FSDescriptor():
4641 ''' Provides information about a particular function space used by
4642 a meta-funcs entry in the kernel metadata. '''
4643
4644 def __init__(self, descriptor):
4645 self._descriptor = descriptor
4646
4647 @property
4648 def requires_basis(self):
4649 ''' Returns True if a basis function is associated with this
4650 function space, otherwise it returns False. '''
4651 return "gh_basis" in self._descriptor.operator_names
4652
4653 @property
4654 def requires_diff_basis(self):
4655 ''' Returns True if a differential basis function is
4656 associated with this function space, otherwise it returns
4657 False. '''
4658 return "gh_diff_basis" in self._descriptor.operator_names
4659
4660 @property
4661 def fs_name(self):
4662 ''' Returns the raw metadata value of this function space. '''
4663 return self._descriptor.function_space_name
4664
4665
4666class FSDescriptors():
4667 ''' Contains a collection of FSDescriptor objects and methods
4668 that provide information across these objects. We have one
4669 FSDescriptor for each meta-funcs entry in the kernel
4670 metadata.
4671 # TODO #274 this should actually be named something like
4672 BasisFuncDescriptors as it holds information describing the
4673 basis/diff-basis functions required by a kernel.
4674
4675 :param descriptors: list of objects describing the basis/diff-basis \
4676 functions required by a kernel, as obtained from \
4677 metadata.
4678 :type descriptors: list of :py:class:`psyclone.DynFuncDescriptor03`.
4679
4680 '''
4681 def __init__(self, descriptors):
4682 self._orig_descriptors = descriptors
4683 self._descriptors = []
4684 for descriptor in descriptors:
4685 self._descriptors.append(FSDescriptor(descriptor))
4686
4687 def exists(self, fspace):
4688 ''' Return True if a descriptor with the specified function
4689 space exists, otherwise return False. '''
4690 for descriptor in self._descriptors:
4691 # FS descriptors hold information taken from the kernel
4692 # metadata and therefore it is the original name of
4693 # the supplied function space that we must look at
4694 if descriptor.fs_name == fspace.orig_name:
4695 return True
4696 return False
4697
4698 def get_descriptor(self, fspace):
4699 ''' Return the descriptor with the specified function space
4700 name. If it does not exist raise an error.'''
4701 for descriptor in self._descriptors:
4702 if descriptor.fs_name == fspace.orig_name:
4703 return descriptor
4704 raise GenerationError(
4705 f"FSDescriptors:get_descriptor: there is no descriptor for "
4706 f"function space {fspace.orig_name}")
4707
4708 @property
4709 def descriptors(self):
4710 '''
4711 :return: the list of Descriptors, one for each of the meta-funcs
4712 entries in the kernel metadata.
4713 :rtype: List of :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.FSDescriptor`
4714 '''
4715 return self._descriptors
4716
4717
4718def check_args(call, parent_call):
4719 '''
4720 Checks that the kernel arguments provided via the invoke call are
4721 consistent with the information expected, as specified by the
4722 kernel metadata.
4723
4724 :param call: the object produced by the parser that describes the
4725 kernel call to be checked.
4726 :type call: :py:class:`psyclone.parse.algorithm.KernelCall`
4727 :param parent_call: the kernel-call object.
4728 :type parent_call: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
4729
4730 :raises: GenerationError if the kernel arguments in the Algorithm layer
4731 do not match up with the kernel metadata.
4732 '''
4733 # stencil arguments
4734 stencil_arg_count = 0
4735 for arg_descriptor in call.ktype.arg_descriptors:
4736 if arg_descriptor.stencil:
4737 if not arg_descriptor.stencil['extent']:
4738 # an extent argument must be provided
4739 stencil_arg_count += 1
4740 if arg_descriptor.stencil['type'] == 'xory1d':
4741 # a direction argument must be provided
4742 stencil_arg_count += 1
4743
4744 const = LFRicConstants()
4745 # Quadrature arguments - will have as many as there are distinct
4746 # quadrature shapes specified in the metadata.
4747 qr_arg_count = len(set(call.ktype.eval_shapes).intersection(
4748 set(const.VALID_QUADRATURE_SHAPES)))
4749
4750 # If a kernel operates on halo columns then it takes an extra, halo-depth
4751 # argument from the Algorithm layer.
4752 halo_depth_count = 0
4753 if "halo" in call.ktype.iterates_over:
4754 halo_depth_count = 1
4755 expected_arg_count = (len(call.ktype.arg_descriptors) +
4756 stencil_arg_count + qr_arg_count + halo_depth_count)
4757
4758 if expected_arg_count != len(call.args):
4759 msg = ""
4760 if parent_call:
4761 invoke = parent_call.ancestor(LFRicInvokeSchedule)
4762 if invoke:
4763 msg = f"from invoke '{invoke.name}' "
4764 raise GenerationError(
4765 f"error: expected '{expected_arg_count}' arguments for the call "
4766 f"to kernel '{call.ktype.name}' {msg}in the algorithm layer but "
4767 f"found '{len(call.args)}'. Expected "
4768 f"'{len(call.ktype.arg_descriptors)}' standard arguments, "
4769 f"'{stencil_arg_count}' stencil arguments, '{qr_arg_count}' "
4770 f"qr_arguments and '{halo_depth_count}' halo-depth arguments.")
4771
4772
4773@dataclass(frozen=True)
4774class LFRicArgStencil:
4775 '''
4776 Provides stencil information about an LFRic kernel argument.
4777 LFRicArgStencil can provide the extent, algorithm argument for the extent,
4778 and the direction argument of a stencil or set any of these properties.
4779
4780 :param name: the name of the stencil.
4781 :param extent: the extent of the stencil if it is known. It will
4782 be known if it is specified in the metadata.
4783 :param extent_arg: the algorithm argument associated with the extent
4784 value if extent was not found in the metadata.
4785 :param direction_arg: the direction argument associated with the
4786 direction of the stencil if the direction of the
4787 stencil is not known.
4788 '''
4789 name: str
4790 extent: str = None
4791 extent_arg: Any = None
4792 direction_arg: Any = None
4793
4794
4795class DynKernelArguments(Arguments):
4796 '''
4797 Provides information about Dynamo kernel call arguments
4798 collectively, as specified by the kernel argument metadata.
4799
4800 :param call: the kernel metadata for which to extract argument info.
4801 :type call: :py:class:`psyclone.parse.KernelCall`
4802 :param parent_call: the kernel-call object.
4803 :type parent_call: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
4804 :param bool check: whether to check for consistency between the
4805 kernel metadata and the algorithm layer. Defaults to True.
4806
4807 :raises GenerationError: if the kernel metadata specifies stencil extent.
4808 '''
4809 def __init__(self, call, parent_call, check=True):
4810 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
4811 if False: # pylint: disable=using-constant-test
4812 # For pyreverse
4813 self._0_to_n = DynKernelArgument(None, None, None, None)
4814
4815 Arguments.__init__(self, parent_call)
4816
4817 # check that the arguments provided by the algorithm layer are
4818 # consistent with those expected by the kernel(s)
4819 check_args(call, parent_call)
4820
4821 # create our arguments and add in stencil information where
4822 # appropriate.
4823 self._args_args_args = []
4824 idx = 0
4825 for arg in call.ktype.arg_descriptors:
4826 dyn_argument = DynKernelArgument(self, arg, call.args[idx],
4827 parent_call, check)
4828 idx += 1
4829 if dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil:
4830 if dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil['extent']:
4831 raise GenerationError("extent metadata not yet supported")
4832 # if supported we would add the following
4833 # line: stencil.extent =
4834 # dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil['extent']
4835 # An extent argument has been added.
4836 stencil_extent_arg = call.args[idx]
4837 idx += 1
4838 if dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil['type'] == 'xory1d':
4839 # a direction argument has been added
4840 stencil = LFRicArgStencil(
4841 name=dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil['type'],
4842 extent_arg=stencil_extent_arg,
4843 direction_arg=call.args[idx]
4844 )
4845 idx += 1
4846 else:
4847 # Create a stencil object and store a reference to it in
4848 # our new DynKernelArgument object.
4849 stencil = LFRicArgStencil(
4850 name=dyn_argument.descriptor.stencil['type'],
4851 extent_arg=stencil_extent_arg
4852 )
4853 dyn_argument.stencil = stencil
4854 self._args_args_args.append(dyn_argument)
4855
4856 # We have now completed the construction of the kernel arguments so
4857 # we can go back and update the names of any stencil size and/or
4858 # direction variable names to ensure there are no clashes.
4859 if self._parent_call_parent_call:
4860 inv_sched = self._parent_call_parent_call.ancestor(InvokeSchedule)
4861 if hasattr(inv_sched, "symbol_table"):
4862 symtab = inv_sched.symbol_table
4863 else:
4864 # This can happen in stub generation.
4865 symtab = LFRicSymbolTable()
4866 else:
4867 # TODO 719 The symtab is not connected to other parts of the
4868 # Stub generation.
4869 symtab = LFRicSymbolTable()
4870 const = LFRicConstants()
4871 for arg in self._args_args_args:
4872 if not arg.descriptor.stencil:
4873 continue
4874 if not arg.stencil.extent_arg.is_literal():
4875 if arg.stencil.extent_arg.varname:
4876 # Ensure extent argument name is registered in the
4877 # symbol_table.
4878 tag = "AlgArgs_" + arg.stencil.extent_arg.text
4879 root = arg.stencil.extent_arg.varname
4880 new_name = symtab.find_or_create_tag(tag, root).name
4881 arg.stencil.extent_arg.varname = new_name
4882 if arg.descriptor.stencil['type'] == 'xory1d':
4883 # a direction argument has been added
4884 if arg.stencil.direction_arg.varname and \
4885 arg.stencil.direction_arg.varname not in \
4886 const.VALID_STENCIL_DIRECTIONS:
4887 # Register the name of the direction argument to ensure
4888 # it is unique in the PSy layer
4889 tag = "AlgArgs_" + arg.stencil.direction_arg.text
4890 root = arg.stencil.direction_arg.varname
4891 new_name = symtab.find_or_create_integer_symbol(
4892 root, tag=tag).name
4893 arg.stencil.direction_arg.varname = new_name
4894
4895 self._dofs = []
4896
4897 # Generate a static list of unique function-space names used
4898 # by the set of arguments: store the mangled names as these
4899 # are what we use at the level of an Invoke
4900 self._unique_fs_names = []
4901 # List of corresponding unique function-space objects
4902 self._unique_fss = []
4903 for arg in self._args_args_args:
4904 for function_space in arg.function_spaces:
4905 # We check that function_space is not None because scalar
4906 # args don't have one and fields only have one (only
4907 # operators have two).
4908 if function_space and \
4909 function_space.mangled_name not in self._unique_fs_names:
4910 self._unique_fs_names.append(function_space.mangled_name)
4911 self._unique_fss.append(function_space)
4912
4913 def get_arg_on_space_name(self, func_space_name):
4914 '''
4915 Returns the first argument (field or operator) found that is on
4916 the named function space, as specified in the kernel metadata. Also
4917 returns the associated FunctionSpace object.
4918
4919 :param str func_space_name: Name of the function space (as specified \
4920 in kernel metadata) for which to \
4921 find an argument.
4922 :return: the first kernel argument that is on the named function \
4923 space and the associated FunctionSpace object.
4924 :rtype: (:py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`,
4925 :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`)
4926 :raises: FieldNotFoundError if no field or operator argument is found \
4927 for the named function space.
4928 '''
4929 for arg in self._args_args_args:
4930 for function_space in arg.function_spaces:
4931 if function_space:
4932 if func_space_name == function_space.orig_name:
4933 return arg, function_space
4934 raise FieldNotFoundError(f"DynKernelArguments:get_arg_on_space_name: "
4935 f"there is no field or operator with "
4936 f"function space {func_space_name}")
4937
4938 def get_arg_on_space(self, func_space):
4939 '''
4940 Returns the first argument (field or operator) found that is on
4941 the specified function space. The mangled name of the supplied
4942 function space is used for comparison.
4943
4944 :param func_space: The function space for which to find an argument.
4945 :type func_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
4946 :return: the first kernel argument that is on the supplied function
4947 space
4948 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
4949 :raises: FieldNotFoundError if no field or operator argument is found
4950 for the specified function space.
4951 '''
4952 for arg in self._args_args_args:
4953 for function_space in arg.function_spaces:
4954 if function_space:
4955 if func_space.mangled_name == function_space.mangled_name:
4956 return arg
4957
4958 raise FieldNotFoundError(f"DynKernelArguments:get_arg_on_space: there "
4959 f"is no field or operator with function space"
4960 f" {func_space.orig_name} (mangled name = "
4961 f"'{func_space.mangled_name}')")
4962
4963 def has_operator(self, op_type=None):
4964 ''' Returns true if at least one of the arguments is an operator
4965 of type op_type (either gh_operator [LMA] or gh_columnwise_operator
4966 [CMA]). If op_type is None then searches for *any* valid operator
4967 type. '''
4968 const = LFRicConstants()
4969 if op_type and op_type not in const.VALID_OPERATOR_NAMES:
4970 raise GenerationError(
4971 f"If supplied, 'op_type' must be a valid operator type (one "
4972 f"of {const.VALID_OPERATOR_NAMES}) but got '{op_type}'")
4973 if not op_type:
4974 # If no operator type is specified then we match any type
4975 op_list = const.VALID_OPERATOR_NAMES
4976 else:
4977 op_list = [op_type]
4978 for arg in self._args_args_args:
4979 if arg.argument_type in op_list:
4980 return True
4981 return False
4982
4983 @property
4984 def unique_fss(self):
4985 ''' Returns a unique list of function space objects used by the
4986 arguments of this kernel '''
4987 return self._unique_fss
4988
4989 @property
4990 def unique_fs_names(self):
4991 ''' Return the list of unique function space names used by the
4992 arguments of this kernel. The names are unmangled (i.e. as
4993 specified in the kernel metadata) '''
4994 return self._unique_fs_names
4995
4996 @property
4997 def first_field_or_operator(self):
4998 '''
4999 :returns: the first field or operator argument in the list.
5000 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
5001
5002 :raises InternalError: if no field or operator argument is found.
5003
5004 '''
5005 for arg in self._args_args_args:
5006 arg: DynKernelArgument
5007 if arg.is_field or arg.is_operator:
5008 return arg
5009
5010 raise InternalError(
5011 f"Invalid LFRic kernel: failed to find a DynKernelArgument that is"
5012 f" a field or operator in '{self.names}'.")
5013
5014 def iteration_space_arg(self):
5015 '''
5016 Returns an argument we can use to dereference the iteration
5017 space. This can be a field or operator that is modified or
5018 alternatively a field that is read if one or more scalars
5019 are modified. If a kernel writes to more than one argument then
5020 that requiring the largest iteration space is selected.
5021
5022 :return: Kernel argument from which to obtain iteration space
5023 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArgument`
5024 '''
5025
5026 # Since we always compute operators out to the L1 halo we first
5027 # check whether this kernel writes to an operator
5028 write_accesses = AccessType.all_write_accesses()
5029 const = LFRicConstants()
5030 op_args = psyGen.args_filter(
5031 self._args_args_args,
5032 arg_types=const.VALID_OPERATOR_NAMES,
5033 arg_accesses=write_accesses)
5034 if op_args:
5035 return op_args[0]
5036
5037 # Is this an inter-grid kernel? If so, then the iteration space
5038 # is determined by the coarse mesh, irrespective of whether
5039 # we are prolonging (and thus writing to a field on the fine mesh)
5040 # or restricting.
5041 if self._parent_call_parent_call.is_intergrid:
5042 fld_args = psyGen.args_filter(
5043 self._args_args_args,
5044 arg_types=const.VALID_FIELD_NAMES,
5045 arg_meshes=["gh_coarse"])
5046 return fld_args[0]
5047
5048 # This is not an inter-grid kernel and it does not write to an
5049 # operator. We now check for fields that are written to. We
5050 # check first for any modified field on a continuous function
5051 # space, failing that we try any_space function spaces
5052 # (because we must assume such a space is continuous) and
5053 # finally we try all discontinuous function spaces including
5054 # any_discontinuous_space. We do this because if a quantity on
5055 # a continuous FS is modified then our iteration space must be
5056 # larger (include L1-halo cells)
5057 const = LFRicConstants()
5058 write_accesses = AccessType.all_write_accesses()
5059 fld_args = psyGen.args_filter(
5060 self._args_args_args,
5061 arg_types=const.VALID_FIELD_NAMES,
5062 arg_accesses=write_accesses)
5063 if fld_args:
5064 for spaces in [const.CONTINUOUS_FUNCTION_SPACES,
5065 const.VALID_ANY_SPACE_NAMES,
5066 const.VALID_DISCONTINUOUS_NAMES]:
5067 for arg in fld_args:
5068 if arg.function_space.orig_name in spaces:
5069 return arg
5070
5071 # No modified fields or operators. Check for unmodified fields...
5072 fld_args = psyGen.args_filter(
5073 self._args_args_args,
5074 arg_types=const.VALID_FIELD_NAMES)
5075 if fld_args:
5076 return fld_args[0]
5077
5078 # it is an error if we get to here
5079 raise GenerationError(
5080 "iteration_space_arg(). The lfric api must have a modified "
5081 "field, a modified operator, or an unmodified field (in the case "
5082 "of a modified scalar). None of these were found.")
5083
5084 @property
5085 def dofs(self):
5086 ''' Currently required for Invoke base class although this
5087 makes no sense for Dynamo. Need to refactor the Invoke base class
5088 and remove the need for this property (#279). '''
5089 return self._dofs
5090
5091 def psyir_expressions(self):
5092 '''
5093 :returns: the PSyIR expressions representing this Argument list.
5094 :rtype: list of :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5095
5096 '''
5097 create_arg_list = KernCallArgList(self._parent_call_parent_call)
5098 create_arg_list.generate()
5099 return create_arg_list.psyir_arglist
5100
5101 @property
5102 def acc_args(self):
5103 '''
5104 :returns: the list of quantities that must be available on an \
5105 OpenACC device before the associated kernel can be launched.
5106 :rtype: list of str
5107
5108 '''
5109 create_acc_arg_list = KernCallAccArgList(self._parent_call_parent_call)
5110 create_acc_arg_list.generate()
5111 return create_acc_arg_list.arglist
5112
5113 @property
5114 def scalars(self):
5115 '''
5116 Provides the list of names of scalar arguments required by the
5117 kernel associated with this Arguments object. If there are none
5118 then the returned list is empty.
5119
5120 :returns: A list of the names of scalar arguments in this object.
5121 :rtype: list of str
5122 '''
5123 # Return nothing for the moment as it is unclear whether
5124 # scalars need to be explicitly dealt with (for OpenACC) in
5125 # the dynamo api.
5126 return []
5127
5128
5129class DynKernelArgument(KernelArgument):
5130 '''
5131 This class provides information about individual LFRic kernel call
5132 arguments as specified by the kernel argument metadata and the
5133 kernel invocation in the Algorithm layer.
5134
5135 :param kernel_args: object encapsulating all arguments to the \
5136 kernel call.
5137 :type kernel_args: :py:class:`psyclone.dynamo0p3.DynKernelArguments`
5138 :param arg_meta_data: information obtained from the metadata for \
5139 this kernel argument.
5140 :type arg_meta_data: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicArgDescriptor`
5141 :param arg_info: information on how this argument is specified in \
5142 the Algorithm layer.
5143 :type arg_info: :py:class:`psyclone.parse.algorithm.Arg`
5144 :param call: the kernel object with which this argument is associated.
5145 :type call: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.LFRicKern`
5146 :param bool check: whether to check for consistency between the \
5147 kernel metadata and the algorithm layer. Defaults to True.
5148
5149 :raises InternalError: for an unsupported metadata in the argument \
5150 descriptor data type.
5151
5152 '''
5153 # pylint: disable=too-many-public-methods, too-many-instance-attributes
5154 def __init__(self, kernel_args, arg_meta_data, arg_info, call, check=True):
5155 # Keep a reference to DynKernelArguments object that contains
5156 # this argument. This permits us to manage name-mangling for
5157 # any-space function spaces.
5158 self._kernel_args = kernel_args
5159 self._vector_size = arg_meta_data.vector_size
5160 self._argument_type = arg_meta_data.argument_type
5161 self._stencil = None
5162 if arg_meta_data.mesh:
5163 self._mesh = arg_meta_data.mesh.lower()
5164 else:
5165 self._mesh = None
5166
5167 # The list of function-space objects for this argument. Each
5168 # object can be queried for its original name and for the
5169 # mangled name (used to make any-space arguments distinct
5170 # within an invoke). The argument will only have more than
5171 # one function-space associated with it if it is an operator.
5172 fs1 = None
5173 fs2 = None
5174
5175 if self.is_operatoris_operatoris_operator:
5176
5177 fs1 = FunctionSpace(arg_meta_data.function_space_to,
5178 self._kernel_args)
5179 fs2 = FunctionSpace(arg_meta_data.function_space_from,
5180 self._kernel_args)
5181 else:
5182 if arg_meta_data.function_space:
5183 fs1 = FunctionSpace(arg_meta_data.function_space,
5184 self._kernel_args)
5185 self._function_spaces = [fs1, fs2]
5186
5187 # Set the argument's intrinsic type from its descriptor's
5188 # data type and check if an invalid data type is passed from
5189 # the argument descriptor.
5190 try:
5191 const = LFRicConstants()
5192 self._intrinsic_type = const.MAPPING_DATA_TYPES[
5193 arg_meta_data.data_type]
5194 except KeyError as err:
5195 raise InternalError(
5196 f"DynKernelArgument.__init__(): Found unsupported data "
5197 f"type '{arg_meta_data.data_type}' in the kernel argument "
5198 f"descriptor '{arg_meta_data}'.") from err
5199
5200 # Addressing issue #753 will allow us to perform static checks
5201 # for consistency between the algorithm and the kernel
5202 # metadata. This will include checking that a field on a read
5203 # only function space is not passed to a kernel that modifies
5204 # it. Note, issue #79 is also related to this.
5205 KernelArgument.__init__(self, arg_meta_data, arg_info, call)
5206 # Argument proxy data type (if/as defined in LFRic infrastructure)
5207 self._proxy_data_type = None
5208 # Set up kernel argument information for scalar, field and operator
5209 # arguments: precision, module name, data type and proxy data type
5210 self._init_data_type_properties(arg_info, check)
5211 # Complete the initialisation of the argument (after
5212 # _init_data_type_properties() so the precision info etc is
5213 # already set up)
5214 self._complete_init(arg_info)
5215
5216 def ref_name(self, function_space=None):
5217 '''
5218 Returns the name used to dereference this type of argument (depends
5219 on whether it is a field or operator and, if the latter, whether it
5220 is the to- or from-space that is specified).
5221
5222 :param function_space: the function space of this argument
5223 :type function_space: :py:class:`psyclone.domain.lfric.FunctionSpace`
5224
5225 :returns: the name used to dereference this argument.
5226 :rtype: str
5227
5228 :raises GenerationError: if the supplied function space is not one \
5229 of the function spaces associated with \
5230 this argument.
5231 :raises GenerationError: if the supplied function space is not being \
5232 returned by either 'function_space_from' or \
5233 'function_space_to'.
5234 :raises GenerationError: if the argument type is not supported.
5235
5236 '''
5237 # pylint: disable=too-many-branches
5238 if not function_space:
5239 if self.is_operatoris_operatoris_operator:
5240 # For an operator we use the 'from' FS
5241 function_space = self._function_spaces[1]
5242 else:
5243 function_space = self._function_spaces[0]
5244 else:
5245 # Check that the supplied function space is valid for this
5246 # argument
5247 found = False
5248 for fspace in self.function_spacesfunction_spaces:
5249 if fspace and fspace.orig_name == function_space.orig_name:
5250 found = True
5251 break
5252 if not found:
5253 raise GenerationError(
5254 f"DynKernelArgument.ref_name(fs): The supplied function "
5255 f"space (fs='{function_space.orig_name}') is not one of "
5256 f"the function spaces associated with this argument "
5257 f"(fss={self.function_space_names}).")
5258 if self.is_fieldis_field:
5259 return "vspace"
5260 if self.is_operatoris_operatoris_operator:
5261 if function_space.orig_name == self.descriptor.function_space_from:
5262 return "fs_from"
5263 if function_space.orig_name == self.descriptor.function_space_to:
5264 return "fs_to"
5265 raise GenerationError(
5266 f"DynKernelArgument.ref_name(fs): Function space "
5267 f"'{function_space.orig_name}' is one of the 'gh_operator' "
5268 f"function spaces '{self.function_spaces}' but is not being "
5269 f"returned by either function_space_from "
5270 f"'{self.descriptor.function_space_from}' or "
5271 f"function_space_to '{self.descriptor.function_space_to}'.")
5272 raise GenerationError(
5273 f"DynKernelArgument.ref_name(fs): Found unsupported argument "
5274 f"type '{self._argument_type}'.")
5275
5276 def _init_data_type_properties(self, arg_info, check=True):
5277 '''Set up kernel argument information from LFRicConstants: precision,
5278 data type, proxy data type and module name. This is currently
5279 supported for scalar, field and operator arguments.
5280
5281 :param arg_info: information on how this argument is specified \
5282 in the Algorithm layer.
5283 :type arg_info: :py:class:`psyclone.parse.algorithm.Arg`
5284 :param bool check: whether to use the algorithm \
5285 information. Optional argument that defaults to True.
5286
5287 '''
5288 alg_datatype_info = None
5289 if arg_info:
5290 alg_datatype_info = arg_info._datatype
5291 alg_datatype = None
5292 alg_precision = None
5293 if alg_datatype_info:
5294 alg_datatype, alg_precision = alg_datatype_info
5295
5296 const = LFRicConstants()
5297 if arg_info and arg_info.form == "collection":
5298 try:
5299 alg_datatype = const.FIELD_VECTOR_TO_FIELD_MAP[alg_datatype]
5300 except KeyError:
5301 # The collection datatype is not recognised or supported.
5302 alg_datatype = None
5303
5304 if self.is_scalaris_scalaris_scalar:
5305 self._init_scalar_properties(alg_datatype, alg_precision,
5306 check)
5307 elif self.is_fieldis_field:
5308 self._init_field_properties(alg_datatype, check)
5309 elif self.is_operatoris_operatoris_operator:
5310 self._init_operator_properties(alg_datatype, check)
5311 else:
5312 raise InternalError(
5313 f"Supported argument types are scalar, field and operator, "
5314 f"but the argument '{self.name}' in kernel "
5315 f"'{self._call.name}' is none of these.")
5316
5317 def _init_scalar_properties(
5318 self, alg_datatype, alg_precision, check=True):
5319 '''Set up the properties of this scalar using algorithm datatype
5320 information if it is available.
5321
5322 :param alg_datatype: the datatype of this argument as \
5323 specified in the algorithm layer or None if it is not \
5324 known.
5325 :type alg_datatype: str or NoneType
5326 :param alg_precision: the precision of this argument as \
5327 specified in the algorithm layer or None if it is not \
5328 known.
5329 :type alg_precision: str or NoneType
5330 :param bool check: whether to use the algorithm \
5331 information. Optional argument that defaults to True.
5332
5333 :raises InternalError: if the intrinsic type of the scalar is \
5334 not supported.
5335 :raises GenerationError: if the datatype specified in the \
5336 algorithm layer is inconsistent with the kernel metadata.
5337 :raises GenerationError: if the datatype for a gh_scalar \
5338 could not be found in the algorithm layer.
5339 :raises NotImplementedError: if the scalar is a reduction and \
5340 its intrinsic type is not real.
5341 :raises GenerationError: if the scalar is a reduction and is \
5342 not declared with default precision.
5343
5344 '''
5345 const = LFRicConstants()
5346 # Check the type of scalar defined in the metadata is supported.
5347 if self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type not in const.VALID_INTRINSIC_TYPES:
5348 raise InternalError(
5349 f"Expected one of {const.VALID_INTRINSIC_TYPES} intrinsic "
5350 f"types for a scalar argument but found "
5351 f"'{self.intrinsic_type}' in the metadata of kernel "
5352 f"{self._call.name} for argument {self.name}.")
5353
5354 # Check the metadata and algorithm types are consistent if
5355 # the algorithm information is available and is not being ignored.
5356 if check and alg_datatype and \
5357 alg_datatype != self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type:
5358 raise GenerationError(
5359 f"The kernel metadata for argument '{self.name}' in "
5360 f"kernel '{self._call.name}' specifies this argument "
5361 f"should be a scalar of type '{self.intrinsic_type}' but "
5362 f"in the algorithm layer it is defined as a "
5363 f"'{alg_datatype}'.")
5364
5365 # If the algorithm information is not being ignored and
5366 # the datatype is known in the algorithm layer and it is
5367 # not a literal then its precision should also be defined.
5368 if check and alg_datatype and not alg_precision and \
5369 not self.is_literalis_literal:
5370 raise GenerationError(
5371 f"LFRic coding standards require scalars to have "
5372 f"their precision defined in the algorithm layer but "
5373 f"'{self.name}' in '{self._call.name}' does not.")
5374
5375 if self.accessaccessaccess in AccessType.get_valid_reduction_modes():
5376 # Treat reductions separately to other scalars as it
5377 # is expected that they should match the precision of
5378 # the field they are reducing. At the moment there is
5379 # an assumption that the precision will always be a
5380 # particular value (the default), see issue #1570.
5381
5382 # Only real reductions are supported.
5383 if not self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "real":
5384 raise NotImplementedError(
5385 "Reductions for datatypes other than real are not yet "
5386 "supported in PSyclone.")
5387
5388 expected_precision = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP["reduction"]["kind"]
5389 # If the algorithm information is not being ignored
5390 # then check that the expected precision and the
5391 # precision defined in the algorithm layer are
5392 # the same.
5393 if check and alg_precision and \
5394 alg_precision != expected_precision:
5395 raise GenerationError(
5396 f"This scalar is a reduction which assumes precision "
5397 f"of type '{expected_precision}' but the algorithm "
5398 f"declares this scalar with precision "
5399 f"'{alg_precision}'.")
5400
5401 # Use the default 'real' scalar reduction properties.
5402 self._precision_precision = expected_precision
5403 self._data_type_data_type = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP["reduction"]["type"]
5404 self._proxy_data_type = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP[
5405 "reduction"]["proxy_type"]
5406 self._module_name_module_name = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP["reduction"]["module"]
5407 else:
5408 # This is a scalar that is not part of a reduction.
5409
5410 if check and alg_precision:
5411 # Use the algorithm precision if it is available
5412 # and not being ignored.
5413 self._precision_precision = alg_precision
5414 else:
5415 # Use default precision for this datatype if the
5416 # algorithm precision is either not available or is
5417 # being ignored.
5418 self._precision_precision = const.SCALAR_PRECISION_MAP[
5419 self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type]

5421 def _init_field_properties(self, alg_datatype, check=True):
5422 '''Set up the properties of this field using algorithm datatype
5423 information if it is available.
5424
5425 :param alg_datatype: the datatype of this argument as \
5426 specified in the algorithm layer or None if it is not \
5427 known.
5428 :type alg_datatype: str or NoneType
5429 :param bool check: whether to use the algorithm \
5430 information. Optional argument that defaults to True.
5431
5432 :raises GenerationError: if the datatype for a gh_field \
5433 could not be found in the algorithm layer.
5434 :raises GenerationError: if the datatype specified in the \
5435 algorithm layer is inconsistent with the kernel metadata.
5436 :raises InternalError: if the intrinsic type of the field is \
5437 not supported (i.e. is not real or integer).
5438
5439 '''
5440 const = LFRicConstants()
5441 argtype = None
5442 # If the algorithm information is not being ignored then
5443 # it must be available.
5444 if check and not alg_datatype:
5445 raise GenerationError(
5446 f"It was not possible to determine the field type from "
5447 f"the algorithm layer for argument '{self.name}' in "
5448 f"kernel '{self._call.name}'.")
5449
5450 # If the algorithm information is not being ignored then
5451 # check the metadata and algorithm type are consistent and
5452 # that the metadata specifies a supported intrinsic type.
5453 if self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "real":
5454 if not check:
5455 # Use the default as we are ignoring any algorithm info
5456 argtype = "field"
5457 elif alg_datatype == "field_type":
5458 argtype = "field"
5459 elif alg_datatype == "r_bl_field_type":
5460 argtype = "r_bl_field"
5461 elif alg_datatype == "r_phys_field_type":
5462 argtype = "r_phys_field"
5463 elif alg_datatype == "r_solver_field_type":
5464 argtype = "r_solver_field"
5465 elif alg_datatype == "r_tran_field_type":
5466 argtype = "r_tran_field"
5467 else:
5468 raise GenerationError(
5469 f"The metadata for argument '{self.name}' in kernel "
5470 f"'{self._call.name}' specifies that this is a real "
5471 f"field, however it is declared as a "
5472 f"'{alg_datatype}' in the algorithm code.")
5473
5474 elif self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "integer":
5475 if check and alg_datatype != "integer_field_type":
5476 raise GenerationError(
5477 f"The metadata for argument '{self.name}' in kernel "
5478 f"'{self._call.name}' specifies that this is an "
5479 f"integer field, however it is declared as a "
5480 f"'{alg_datatype}' in the algorithm code.")
5481 argtype = "integer_field"
5482 else:
5483 raise InternalError(
5484 f"Expected one of {const.VALID_FIELD_INTRINSIC_TYPES} "
5485 f"intrinsic types for a field argument but found "
5486 f"'{self.intrinsic_type}'.")
5487 self._data_type_data_type = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP[argtype]["type"]
5488 self._precision_precision = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP[argtype]["kind"]
5489 self._proxy_data_type = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP[argtype]["proxy_type"]
5490 self._module_name_module_name = const.DATA_TYPE_MAP[argtype]["module"]

5639 def psyir_expression(self):
5640 '''
5641 Looks up or creates a reference to a suitable Symbol for this kernel
5642 argument. If the argument is a scalar that has been provided as a
5643 literal (in the Algorithm layer) then the PSyIR of the expression
5644 is returned.
5645
5646 :returns: the PSyIR for this kernel argument.
5647 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.nodes.Node`
5648
5649 :raises InternalError: if this argument is a literal but we fail to \
5650 construct PSyIR that is consistent with this.
5651 :raises NotImplementedError: if this argument is not a literal, scalar
5652 or field.
5653
5654 '''
5655 symbol_table = self._call.scope.symbol_table
5656
5657 if self.is_literalis_literal:
5658 reader = FortranReader()
5659 if self.precisionprecision:
5660 # Ensure any associated precision symbol is in the table.
5661 symbol_table.add_lfric_precision_symbol(self.precisionprecision)
5662 lit = reader.psyir_from_expression(self.name, symbol_table)
5663
5664 # Sanity check that the resulting expression is a literal.
5665 if lit.walk(Reference):
5666 raise InternalError(
5667 f"Expected argument '{self.name}' to kernel "
5668 f"'{self.call.name}' to be a literal but the created "
5669 f"PSyIR contains one or more References.")
5670 return lit
5671
5672 if self.is_scalaris_scalaris_scalar:
5673 try:
5674 scalar_sym = symbol_table.lookup(self.name)
5675 except KeyError:
5676 # TODO once #1258 is done the symbols should already exist
5677 # and therefore we should raise an exception if not.
5678 scalar_sym = symbol_table.new_symbol(
5679 self.name, symbol_type=DataSymbol,
5680 datatype=self.infer_datatypeinfer_datatype())
5681 return Reference(scalar_sym)
5682
5683 const = LFRicConstants()
5684 try:
5685 suffix = const.ARG_TYPE_SUFFIX_MAPPING[self.argument_typeargument_typeargument_type]
5686 tag_name = f"{self.name}:{suffix}"
5687 sym = symbol_table.lookup_with_tag(tag_name)
5688 return Reference(sym)
5689
5690 except KeyError as err:
5691 raise NotImplementedError(
5692 f"Unsupported kernel argument type: '{self.name}' is of type "
5693 f"'{self.argument_type}' which is not recognised as being a "
5694 f"literal, scalar or field.") from err

5875 def infer_datatype(self, proxy=False):
5876 '''
5877 Infer the datatype of this kernel argument in the PSy layer using
5878 the LFRic API rules. If any LFRic infrastructure modules are required
5879 but are not already present then suitable ContainerSymbols are added
5880 to the outermost symbol table. Similarly, DataTypeSymbols are added for
5881 any required LFRic derived types that are not already in the symbol
5882 table.
5883
5884 TODO #1258 - ultimately this routine should not have to create any
5885 DataTypeSymbols as that should already have been done.
5886
5887 :param bool proxy: whether or not we want the type of the proxy \
5888 object for this kernel argument. Defaults to False (i.e.
5889 return the type rather than the proxy type).
5890
5891 :returns: the datatype of this argument.
5892 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataType`
5893
5894 :raises NotImplementedError: if an unsupported argument type is found.
5895
5896 '''
5897 scope = self._call.ancestor(Container)
5898 if scope is None:
5899 # Prefer the module scope, but some tests that are disconnected can
5900 # use the current scope
5901 scope = self._call.scope
5902
5903 symtab = scope.symbol_table
5904
5905 def _find_or_create_type(mod_name, type_name):
5906 '''
5907 Utility to find or create a DataTypeSymbol with the supplied name,
5908 imported from the named module.
5909
5910 :param str mod_name: the name of the module from which the \
5911 DataTypeSymbol should be imported.
5912 :param str type_name: the name of the derived type for which to \
5913 create a DataTypeSymbol.
5914
5915 :returns: the symbol for the requested type.
5916 :rtype: :py:class:`psyclone.psyir.symbols.DataTypeSymbol`
5917
5918 '''
5919 return symtab.find_or_create(
5920 type_name,
5921 symbol_type=DataTypeSymbol,
5922 datatype=UnresolvedType(),
5923 interface=ImportInterface(symtab.find_or_create(
5924 mod_name,
5925 symbol_type=ContainerSymbol)
5926 ))
5927
5928 if self.is_scalaris_scalaris_scalar:
5929 # Find or create the DataType for the appropriate scalar type.
5930 if self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "real":
5931 prim_type = ScalarType.Intrinsic.REAL
5932 elif self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "integer":
5933 prim_type = ScalarType.Intrinsic.INTEGER
5934 elif self.intrinsic_typeintrinsic_typeintrinsic_type == "logical":
5935 prim_type = ScalarType.Intrinsic.BOOLEAN
5936 else:
5937 raise NotImplementedError(
5938 f"Unsupported scalar type '{self.intrinsic_type}'")
5939
5940 kind_name = self.precisionprecision
5941 try:
5942 kind_symbol = symtab.lookup(kind_name)
5943 except KeyError:
5944 mod_map = LFRicConstants().UTILITIES_MOD_MAP
5945 const_mod = mod_map["constants"]["module"]
5946 try:
5947 constants_container = symtab.lookup(const_mod)
5948 except KeyError:
5949 # TODO Once #696 is done, we should *always* have a
5950 # symbol for this container at this point so should
5951 # raise an exception if we haven't.
5952 constants_container = LFRicTypes(const_mod)
5953 symtab.add(constants_container)
5954 kind_symbol = DataSymbol(
5955 kind_name, INTEGER_TYPE,
5956 interface=ImportInterface(constants_container))
5957 symtab.add(kind_symbol)
5958 return ScalarType(prim_type, kind_symbol)
5959
5960 if self.is_fieldis_field or self.is_operatoris_operatoris_operator:
5961 # Find or create the DataTypeSymbol for the appropriate
5962 # field or operator type.
5963 mod_name = self._module_name_module_name
5964 if proxy:
5965 type_name = self._proxy_data_type
5966 else:
5967 type_name = self._data_type_data_type
5968 return _find_or_create_type(mod_name, type_name)
5969
5970 raise NotImplementedError(
5971 f"'{str(self)}' is not a scalar, field or operator argument")
